name: Ambient 3D world loop
description: A WebGL scene fills the hero (100svh) and idles on a clock with no input: a room, a slope of terrain, a water plane or a table of props, drawn in flat palette colours (the ground tone, the surface tone, one accent object). Slow things move: a camera drift of 1-2% amplitude on a 12-20s sine, a few flat opaque planes of a lighter tone sweeping across over 20-40s, ripples on a water plane. The hero headline sits at the display step (two lines at most) at the bottom-left on the scene's calm part, directly on it with no box, with the dealt button beside it. The next section stands on the flat ground and scrolls over the scene, so long text never depends on it. The loop pauses when the tab is hidden or the canvas is off screen. Colour roles: ground = the scene's dominant tone, ink contrasting, accent = one lit object.
signature: The first screen's backdrop is a live 3D room, slope or water that drifts by itself (camera swaying 1-2%, flat light planes sliding) with the headline at the bottom-left directly on it.
phone: Camera drift off, pixel ratio 1.5; with reduced motion render one still frame.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: dust motes (particles), translucent light shafts (glass and gradient read) and cards laid over the scene; light is a flat opaque plane with no glow.

name: Bent planes on a ring
description: Six to eight portrait picture cards (3:4, about 320x430 on screen) are mapped onto planes bent around a ring or arc in WebGL (radius 1200-1800px, cards facing outward). The centred card is full size and its neighbours recede with depth, darker, at 0.55 opacity. The section is a held stage of about a third of a screen of scroll per card (about two and a half screens in all); each time the scroll crosses the next step the ring turns one card over 900ms (ease-out-expo), and two text controls, Previous and Next, in the dealt second-action style and the arrow keys do the same. The wheel is never captured, and the ring rests still between steps. The centred card's title at the sub step and one body-step line sit beneath in DOM text on the ground. Colour roles: flat ground, ink, the accent on the controls' arrow glyphs only.
phone: Native scroll steps it, radius 900px, five cards visible; with reduced motion the same cards in a plain two-across grid.
houseRuleCheck: No counter or index between cards and no drag cue; pictures must not be documentary photographs; no text boxes on the cards; designed out: depth blur on the pictures, the 56px circle buttons and the click-to-open card.

name: Scroll camera flight
description: One fixed full-viewport WebGL canvas holds a continuous world (terrain, a corridor of columns, a field of objects, a city of blocks built from plain geometry or a few loaded models) behind a held stage. A camera flies through it on a baked spline: the stage's scroll progress 0-1 over 2-3 screens maps to the spline position through a 0.06-0.1 lerp so it glides. The world is lit flat: ground, fog and sky are palette tones (the ground, the surface tone, the ink), with fog covering 30-80% of the camera range for depth. Three or four text beats of 3-8 words, each a headline at the head step (two lines at most), sit directly on a calm part of the frame with no box, one stop per screen so no held screen is empty, each changing with the progress (in over 0.6 of a screen, out over 0.4); the last stop carries the dealt button. Budget under 150k triangles and compressed textures. Colour roles: ground = the fog tone, ink contrasting, accent = one lit object.
phone: Pixel ratio capped at 1.5, fewer objects, scroll length cut to about 60%; beats at the head step; with reduced motion show a still frame and the beats as ordinary sections.
houseRuleCheck: Fog and sky are flat tones, no gradient sky, glow or glass; beats sit straight on the canvas with no box; the flight is cut from 6-8 screens to 2-3. Dealt only where the builder has a 3D scene it can honestly make.

name: Chapter scene backdrop
description: A fixed WebGL layer sits behind one stretch of the page. Three or four chapters, each 100-130vh tall, own one scene built from instanced photographs (image planes), cut-outs or type glyphs of the page's own words: a drifting field of tiles, a low landscape of cut-outs, a swarm of words. Scenes regroup rather than cut: the instances tween for 1.2-1.6s (ease-in-out) into the next layout when the next chapter crosses the middle of the screen, while the ground changes between the dealt ground, the surface tone and the ink field (flat, never a gradient). DOM text scrolls over it: a chapter statement at the head step (two lines at most) and body text at the body step in lines of at most 44 characters, with the dealt gap between chapters. Ink flips light or dark with the ground (contrast 4.5:1 or better). Colour roles: the dealt ground, surface tone and ink field; accent on one instanced object at most.
phone: Instance count x0.4, pixel ratio 1.5, same chapters with statements at the head step; with reduced motion swap scenes by a 200ms fade.
houseRuleCheck: Instances are photographs, cut-outs or type glyphs; loose decorative discs, blobs and drawn shapes are dropped; tones change flat, never as a gradient, and the photographs carry the colour (no wall of tiles in several fills).

name: Click camera dive
description: A 3D scene (a gallery of frames, a row of doors, a shelf of objects, a miniature town) rests in a stage 80-100svh tall in a slow idle drift. Clicking an object tweens the camera along a baked path into it over 1.2-2s (ease-in-out) while the others fade to the ground tone, and it ends on a flat detail scene holding a headline at the head step (two lines at most), a lead-step line and the dealt button. A text Back link returns by the reverse path in 1.2s. Hovered objects lift 4% with the cursor. A plain list of the same objects as text links stands under the stage as the fallback for no-script, touch and screen readers. Colour roles: ground = the scene's flat tone, objects supply the colour, ink contrasting, accent on the button only.
phone: Tap to dive over 1.2s, pixel ratio 1.5; with reduced motion cut instead of travelling.
houseRuleCheck: Flat ground and fog, no glow and no gradient sky; the overlay text sits directly on the flat detail scene with no box on a photograph; the dive stays under 2s.

name: Click weather switch
description: A stage 85svh tall holding a live 3D scene supplied for the page (the subject's object or place), with one flat sky colour and linear fog toward that colour, camera fixed at a 12-degree look-down. Three states are chosen with three buttons in a row at the bottom centre, 16px apart (the active state in the dealt button, the other two in the dealt second-action style). On click, over 1.6s: the sky and fog colour lerp to the new state's colours, the fog density lerps (0.012 to 0.04) and the scene rotates 25 degrees about the vertical axis; no particles, no lightning. Colour: each state is one sky colour plus one fog colour taken from the scene's own palette; the page ground stays the section's own.
phone: The three buttons share the width in equal thirds at the bottom, 52px high, 32px above the safe area; pixel ratio capped at 1.5.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the snow or rain particle layer, a world drawn just for the page (a supplied 3D scene is needed) and own pills (the dealt button). Sky is one flat colour per state, no gradient skybox; no text box over the scene.

name: Clock day-night cycle
description: A modelled 3D diorama (one cluster of objects on a base, 100svh stage) is lit by four presets keyed to the visitor's local clock: day (6-17h), dusk (17-20h), night (20-5h), dawn (5-6h), with light colour, fog colour and rim colour cross-fading over 20-40s at the boundaries (a four-minute accelerated loop when demonstrating). The stage takes its flat colours from the page's own palette: day is the page ground with the ink, night the ink field with ground-coloured letters, dusk and dawn the surface tone; the page itself never changes palette. Every colour is flat per preset; the fog is a flat colour equal to the stage ground and there is no gradient sky. At night stars appear as 1-2px points and lamps light up; small objects (birds, boats, steam) loop. The camera holds with a +-2 degree idle drift. A single headline of 2-5 words at the display step (two lines at most) sits at the left. Phone: 0.75 pixel ratio, static camera.
phone: 0.75 pixel ratio, static camera.
houseRuleCheck: Clean with discipline: no gradient sky or fog, lighting only; the four presets use the page's own ground, ink and surface tone, so there is no second palette and no colour sprawl. Needs a modelled asset, not a drawn illustration.

name: Disc mask world reveal
description: A 100svh stage after the hero holds a 3D world (a floor and 6-12 objects) visible only inside a circular mask at the canvas centre; outside it the canvas is the flat ground. The disc rests at about 60 percent of the viewport height in diameter from the first frame, and a heading at the head step (two lines at most) stands at the left margin. On click or press the mask widens to cover the full screen over 1.6s (expo in-out, no overshoot) while the camera pulls back by 20 percent, revealing the whole world; a second click closes it. The mask edge is a crisp cut with no glow and no outline. The dealt button below the disc says what to do in sentence case (Open the world, then Close). The pointer is the native one. Phone: disc diameter 80 percent of the width, tap to widen.
phone: Disc 80 percent of the width, tap to widen.
houseRuleCheck: Clean with a crisp edge: a glowing rim would be a glow and an outline, so the edge is a plain mask cut, and the disc neither overshoots nor breathes. The world is modelled 3D, not a drawn illustration, and nothing grows on load (the dealt entrance decides).

name: Hotspot model explorer
description: A pinned stage of about 2 screens of scroll built around one supplied 3D model (a product or object, about 70vh tall) on a flat ground. First half: a two-line headline at the display step and a one-line sub stand at the left, the model right of centre, nothing over the model. At 50% of the scroll the text steps aside (fades out over 300px of scroll) and the model moves to the centre. From then the visitor can orbit it with the arrow keys or a pointer drag on the model (damped 0.08, vertical angle clamped to 20 degrees), and 4 to 6 hotspots (ink discs 28px with a plus glyph in the ground colour, still, projected from fixed points on the model) can be clicked. A click eases the camera to a preset view in 0.9s, the open disc takes the accent, and a card in the dealt card style (surface fill, 320px wide, 24px padding, a title at the sub step, two lines of 16px text) opens in a fixed column at the right of the stage, never over the model; no leader lines.
phone: Orbit by a previous and next button pair that steps the camera presets (a drag orbit only after a first tap on the model, otherwise the page scrolls); hotspots are 44px targets; the card docks under the stage inside the page margins.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: a headline over the model, accent on every hotspot (only the open one takes it) and a card over the model; the pin was 300vh and is two screens. The drag here is a 3D orbit, not a rail; no leader lines.

name: Idle float loop
description: One object (a cut-out product picture or a modelled product) hangs in the middle of a section and never stops moving: a vertical bob of about 10px on a 4-6s sine (ease-in-out), a slower sideways drift of 6px on a 7s sine and a rotation of +-2 degrees. In WebGL it is the mesh transform; in the DOM a CSS keyframe on transform with will-change. The loop pauses when off screen and under reduced motion. No shadow under or behind the object at rest and no box around it. Phone: the same with 30 percent less amplitude.
phone: Same, 30 percent less amplitude.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. No shadow at rest, no drawn shapes, no card around the object; the motion is slow and never jerky.

name: Intro camera pullback
description: A hero whose 3D canvas starts with the camera close (a macro of one object, or inside a tunnel of ribbons) and dollies back along its axis over 1-3s (power1 in-out; for example camera distance growing about 20 percent, say 21 to 25.5 in scene measure, at a 25 degree field of view) to a wide composition where the whole set reads. The move is inside the canvas: the headline (display step, 2-5 words, two lines at most), the navigation and the one action are HTML over it, finished and readable from the first frame, on a calm part of the picture. Props or picture planes rush past the lens in the first 40 percent. The camera then holds with a +-1 degree idle sway. The first screen is the canvas and the headline alone, and nothing of the next section shows. Any input skips to the end in 300ms. Phone: 1.2s, lower resolution, same end frame.
phone: 1.2s, lower resolution, same end frame.
houseRuleCheck: Clean when the headline is there from the first frame: the camera move never holds the words back; it is motion inside the media, skippable, under 3s, ending on a full-screen hero alone.

name: Cut-out layers fly forward
description: A deep collage that the scroll flies through. The first screen is a finished collage on the ground (a CSS 3D stage with perspective 1200px, or WebGL): 5 to 6 flat cut-outs (transparent PNGs of products, objects or portraits, 200 to 520px) at resting depths between 0 and -400, leaving the centre 640x360 free for the title (display step, one or two words, readable at once). The planes shift with the pointer by depth (translate = depth factor x pointer x 20px, eased 0.06). Over the first 600px of scroll (scrubbed, no pin) the camera flies forward: each plane moves toward the viewer by its depth (translateZ up to +900, the nearest passing out of frame first), the title lifts out and the hero scrolls away under the flying planes. Colour: ground flat; the cut-outs carry all other colour; ink for the title.
phone: 4 planes at 120 to 260px; no pointer parallax (a slow 10s sway of 8px instead); title at the display step.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the 2.2s load intro and its burst variant (the first frame is the finished collage and arrives with the dealt entrance) and 12 to 16 planes (a page has 3 to 6 pictures). Cut-outs are photographs or generated imagery, never drawn illustrations; no boxes on the pictures; the hero still fills the first screen alone.

name: Scroll-posed 3D model
description: A sticky stage of 100svh inside 200-250vh of scroll holds one live 3D model (a product, a device, a vessel, a figure; 20-80k triangles, flat-lit) centred at about 55% of the stage height. Its pose is a function of scroll progress through a 0.08 lerp: yaw 0 to 360 degrees, a lid opening 0 to 90, an exploded view separating parts by up to 120px. Three or four short beats (up to 10 words, each a headline at the head step, two lines at most) alternate left and right of the model at about 14% and 62% of the width and change with progress. Colour roles: a flat ground tone chosen as the model's complement, ink contrasting, accent = one part of the model plus the dealt button at the end.
phone: Model at 55% height at the top with the beats beneath at the head step; pin 160vh, pixel ratio 1.5; with reduced motion show one static pose and the beats as plain blocks.
houseRuleCheck: No cast shadow, glow rim or gradient backdrop; the ground is flat and the model carries no text box; the pin is cut from 250-400vh to 200-250vh. Dealt only where the page has a 3D model.

name: Models drop in spinning
description: Three to five solid product models (each about 22% of the stage height) stand in a row on a fixed stage with 60-100px gaps, in place from the first frame (the models arrive with the dealt entrance; under already-there nothing falls in). The camera is still. The first screen is the stage: a headline at the display step (two lines at most) sits behind the models (overlapped by at most 15%) with the dealt button beneath. The models idle with a 4px bob; on hover a model lifts 3-4% and spins one full turn over 800ms on ease-out (0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), and a tap triggers the spin on touch. Colour roles: flat ground, ink, the models bring the colours, the accent on the dealt button.
signature: The first screen's stage holds three to five solid product models in a row, bobbing 4px and spinning one full turn when hovered, with the headline partly behind them (overlap at most 15%).
phone: The row becomes a 2 plus 1 arrangement at 60% size; with reduced motion no bob or spin.
houseRuleCheck: No cast shadows or glow; the headline stays readable; designed out: the load drop-and-spin intro (arrival belongs to the dealt entrance), so the id's drop is not built.

name: Particle shape morph
description: A point cloud of 8,000-30,000 round points (2-3px) fills a fixed canvas stage (100svh) for a pin of 2-3 viewport heights, the points in the ink on the ground (or ground on ink) with the accent for a single chapter. Per scroll chapter (three chapters of about 0.8 viewport each) the cloud morphs between three forms sampled once in a worker from the page's own words (the name, the promise word, the result), never an abstract sphere or ring. Each morph takes 1.2-1.8s (power2 in-out) with each point on a curved path, 0-300ms of random delay and a scale of 1 to 1.4 midway. A heading at the head step (two lines at most) and one caption of at most 15 words at the body step sit at the left in HTML. The first form is already assembled at the first frame, and the pin releases after the last. Phone: 6,000-12,000 points, portrait framing, cloud 70 percent of the width.
phone: 6,000-12,000 points, portrait framing.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. The points are rendered dots, not drawn line art or an illustration; no white flash; chapters are not numbered and no progress rail shows them; the pin is at most three screens and releases.

name: Scroll relight
description: A pinned 3D scene of about 1800px of scroll (two screens) with the camera fixed. One supplied 3D object (a device, case, chair or bottle, about 60vh tall) stands on a flat ground plane. A single time-of-day value is scrubbed 0 to 1 over the first 900px: the key light turns through three of the palette's own tones, the ground steps from the dealt ground to the ink field in flat stages, the object's materials take the light's tone and any emissive part (a screen or lamp) brightens from 0.2 to 1; the cast shadow rotates about 60 degrees and lengthens about 2.4 times. Two captions (two lines each, at the sub step, at the left page margin) swap at 33% and 66% with a 400ms fade. The geometry never moves. Colour: light and ground carry the colour change, accent = the emissive part.
phone: Same scene with a 1024 shadow map; captions below the stage in the dealt card style; range 1400px.
houseRuleCheck: Pin is two screens; captions fade (no rise). The rendered shadow is scene lighting, not a UI drop shadow: every caption and card stays flat. The ground changes by flat tone, not by a page gradient.

name: Velocity-driven spin
description: A 3D object (a bottle, a coin, a sculpture, or a ring of 12-24 photograph sprites) idles at 0.1-0.25 rad per second. Scroll speed adds angular velocity (velocity x 0.0006 rad per px/s, capped at 3x idle) in the direction of scroll and eases back to idle with damping 0.94 per frame. It sits in the hero or a section about 100vh tall at 55-65% of the viewport height with a headline at the display step (two lines at most) behind it. Colour roles: flat ground, the object brings the colour, ink contrasting, the accent on the dealt button.
phone: Pixel ratio 1.5 and 40% of the sprites; touch swipes add velocity; with reduced motion no spin.
houseRuleCheck: Sprites are photographs or cut-outs, not drawn shapes; no glow and no shadow; designed out: pointer drag (no drag cue) and the 150vh section (content height only).

name: Tiles snap together
description: 24-60 3D tiles (flat planes, each a slice of one picture of the page) fly into one form: the picture they were cut from, laid as a flat wall. Each tile starts a few tile-widths out with a random rotation and rises into place over 700ms (power3 out), top tiles first with a 20-40ms stagger downward. It assembles once, scrubbed over one viewport of scroll as the section arrives, and comes apart only in reverse; it ends as the whole picture, still, in the page's one grade. The camera sits still or sways +-1 degree. Phone: 24 tiles.
phone: 24 tiles, same assembly.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Tiles are slices of one picture, never drawn illustration, with no outlines and no fills in several colours; no endless explode-and-reassemble loop; it ends as one finished picture.

name: Surface cracks apart
description: A pinned scene of about 1800px of scroll (two screens), scrubbed. One large photograph (2:1, 1200x600, centred, inside the page margins) is cut into 24 to 40 irregular tiles along baked crack lines (a Voronoi cut in the mesh), all textured from the same picture so at rest it looks whole. From progress 0.15 the tiles break from a crack origin outward in order: each shrinks to 0.85, tilts up to 12 degrees on two axes and drifts away from the centre by 0 to 3 tile widths, staggered by distance from the origin, revealing the ground between. The camera dollies forward along a short path (z 8 to 4) with a 3-degree roll. From 60% a headline (two lines at the display step) stands in the opened gap; the section releases at the end. Colour: ground = the ink; the photograph supplies the colour; the headline in the ground's contrast colour.
phone: 16 tiles; picture the full width minus the page margins; range 1400px; headline below the stage.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the 2400px pin (two screens), 40 to 70 tiles (24 to 40) and the 80px headline (display step). Cracks are gaps that show the ground, not drawn lines; no outlines on tiles; the tiles are one picture, not several fills.

name: Labels pinned to 3D
description: A pinned 3D scene (a globe or a modelled object; 2-3 viewport heights of scroll) moves with scroll while 4-8 HTML labels track points on it. Every frame each label's screen position is projected from its 3D anchor, so a label can travel up to 1800px across the viewport, staggered, as the object turns; it fades from 0.4 to 1 as its anchor faces the camera and to 0 behind it. A label is a block 36px tall in the dealt corner at the body step in sentence case, 1-3 words, ink fill with ground-coloured letters, attached to its anchor by a 10px dot in the ink (the accent on the one facing the camera) with the label 14px to its right (flipping left near the edge); there is no leader line. Phone: five labels at most, 32px tall, only anchors near the middle.
phone: Five labels at most, 32px pills, near-centre anchors only.
houseRuleCheck: Clean with a dot and a solid label in place of leader lines (hairline rules), and no faint ghost words behind the scene. One accent dot at a time, never a wall of accent. Labels are sentence case at 16px, not tiny uppercase; the pin is at most three screens.

name: Camera steps between rooms
description: A pinned 3D scene in one canvas holds three or four named stops (rooms, floors, camera positions), 2-3 viewport heights of scroll in all (about 0.7 screen per stop). When the scroll crosses a stop's threshold the camera tweens to it in 1s (in-out cubic) as a timed move, and the arrow keys or a click on a hotspot do the same; the wheel is never captured and the page keeps its native scroll. At each stop a caption block appears at the left 600ms after the camera settles (a heading of 2-4 words at the head step and one lead-step line) while the previous one leaves in 200ms. Hotspots are 44px markers in the ink that show one word on hover, the current stop's in the accent. After the last stop the stage releases and the page scrolls on. A visible Next in the dealt button is the fallback for keyboard and mouse. Phone: vertical swipe, 48px hotspots.
phone: Native scroll steps it, 48px hotspots, visible Next button.
houseRuleCheck: Clean on native scroll: no wheel capture, no stop counter, no dot rail for the stops; the stage releases after the last stop and the pin is at most three screens.

name: Arrow-stepped card row
description: A row of four to six filled cards in the dealt card style (surface tone, dealt corner; each about a third of the width inside the page margins less two 24px gaps, a 4:3 picture on top, a lead-step title and a two-line body-step text), three whole cards in view and the rest clipped out at the row's edges with no card cut in half. The section heading at the head step stands on the left, and two text controls, Previous and Next, in the dealt second-action style (label with its typed arrow glyph) sit top-right level with it. A click advances one card (width plus gap) over 600-700ms on ease-out (0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); at either end the control drops to 30% opacity. Keyboard arrows work. Colour roles: flat ground, cards on the surface tone, ink, accent only on the closing link.
signature: Three whole filled cards in a row, stepped one card at a time by Previous and Next text controls beside the heading, nothing cut off at the edges and the end control dimmed to 30%.
phone: The cards stack in one column, 16px apart, with the controls hidden.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the 56px circle buttons (the controls follow the dealt button), the peeking next card, any index counter and drag cue; the row clips at the page margins, never at one screen edge.

name: Hero product switcher
description: A hero (100svh) shows exactly one product at the centre (a cut-out picture, 520-640px tall) on the page ground. Two text links with typeset arrows (Previous, Next; 44px targets) at the left and right edges, inside the page margin, plus the arrow keys (and a swipe on touch), swap to the next of four to six variants: the old product slides out by 24 percent of its width and fades in 300ms while the new one enters from the other side, 80px offset, in 700ms (expo-out); the ground steps between the page ground and the surface tone in 600ms. The page's one headline (display step, two lines at most, says what the brand is) stays in place at the left; the product's name (sub step, 1-3 words) and one lead-step line roll in through a mask in 400ms, and the dealt button stays. There is no autoplay. The first frame is the finished first screen with the first product in place. Phone: product 60 percent of the width, swipe plus the two links at the bottom corners.
signature: The first screen is one centred cut-out product 520-640px tall between two arrow links set inside the page margins; each press slides the product out and the next in over 700ms while its name rolls through a mask, and nothing advances by itself.
phone: Product 60 percent wide, swipe plus the two links at the bottom corners.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Ground swaps are two flat tones, never gradients and never one colour per product (the product's own colour comes from the cut-out); no dots or counters; arrows are filled buttons in the dealt corner, not outlined. It steps by its arrows, keys or a swipe on touch, never by a mouse drag and never on a timer.

name: Vertical wrap wheel
description: A pinned stage of about 2 screens of scroll whose scroll position moves a vertical column of 5 poster cells (photographs or designed 3:4 pictures) that wraps in Y. Cells are 520x680 with a 24px gap, centred right of centre; the active cell at scale 1, the neighbours above and below at 0.82 and 50% opacity. Scroll maps to column offset with lerp 0.05, about 40% of a screen per cell; 140ms after input stops the column settles onto the nearest whole cell (ease-out 500ms); the arrow keys step one cell. At the left a caption block (a title at the head step, two lines of body text, one text link) swaps with a mask roll when the active cell changes (24px rise, 300ms). No drag handler on mouse or touch: scroll or keys only. The stage releases after the last cell. Colour: ground as dealt; the pictures carry the colour; accent = the link.
phone: Column centred at about 72% of the width, cells 260x360, caption under the stage in the dealt card style; scroll maps the same way.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the 600vh pin and 8 to 12 cells (about two screens, 5 cells). Scroll and keys move the column and nothing is dragged, so there is no drag rail; the stage releases at its end and the wheel is never captured.

name: Click image burst
description: A small click reaction on a word or the dealt button (a category name, a primary action). On click 8 to 12 small round-cropped pictures (48 to 72px, cut from 3 pictures made for this move: crops of the subject's details that appear nowhere else on the page; never plain tint discs, never emoji) burst from the click point in a 120-degree upward arc, travelling 50 to 100px (randomised) while scaling 0.3 to 1.2 over 0.9s power2.out and fading out after 0.4s; the elements are pooled and removed on finish. The clicked word dips 4% and returns in 200ms. Colour: the pictures carry the colour; ground and ink unchanged; no accent. Under reduced motion skip the burst and keep the dip.
phone: 6 to 8 pictures at 40 to 56px; fires on tap; no hover state.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: reusing the page's own pictures as crops (each photograph once) and tint discs. The round crops carry no outline; it is feedback on a click, not a particle layer.

name: Card widens on select
description: A row of 4 cards in the dealt card style (its fill and corner) across the content width, 560px high, 16px apart. The selected card takes 42% of the row and shows its photograph running to the card's edges over the top 65%, fading in and scaling 1.2 to 1 over 700ms, with its text in the card's fill below it (a title at the sub step, two lines of 16px text, the dealt button); the others share the rest equally (about 170px each) and show only their fill with the title at the top, two lines at 16px or more. Select by click or tap on a card, or with the arrow keys; widths animate with cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) over 700ms and the active card's text rises 24px and fades in after 300ms. Colour: the surface tone for every card, ink for text, accent only on the dealt button.
phone: Vertical accordion: cards stacked 12px apart; the selected one grows from 96px to 420px tall with the same photograph fade; tap selects; one open at a time.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: text laid on the picture (the text sits in the card's fill), tints from one hue family (one surface tone), the chips and circle arrows (one control set) and the 20px radius (the dealt corner). Cards are fills; no drag, no rail.

name: Click theme switch
description: A product hero with a colourway switch. Three pictures of the same product in three colourways, identical framing. A row of three filled swatches (44px circles, 12px apart, bottom left of the hero at the page margin, each in its colourway's colour; the active one scales to 1.2, no ring) or the arrow keys switch the picture. Over 700ms the picture crossfades to the new colourway (a plain crossfade, never a hue rotation). The page's ground, ink and accent do not change; only the product picture does. Remember the choice in localStorage.
phone: Swatches 40px in a row above the safe area, centred; crossfade 500ms.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: three page themes (the dealt palette stays, one accent hue) and retinted cards and tiles. Swatches are product colours, filled, with no rings; none violet or lavender.

name: Liquid pour on press
description: A product action that triggers a 3s liquid render. A product cut-out (a can, bottle or jar, about 560px tall) stands centred with the dealt button under it. A press starts a WebGL fluid pour (a small stable-fluid solver on a 256x256 grid, splats from the product's opening) in one flat accent colour, with no specular and no transparency; the pour fills the screen from the bottom in 1.6s. The liquid texture is then reused as the transition mask: the next section is revealed wherever the liquid has been, over 1.2s. No text sits on the liquid. Colour: ground as dealt, liquid = the accent, the product carries its own colours.
phone: Without a fast GPU use a flat accent clip-path rise from the bottom (1.2s); fluid only on devices that hold 60fps in a short benchmark.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the round button at the opening (the dealt button is the trigger), the optional sound and the specular shading. The liquid is one flat accent colour, never glassy or gradient-shaded; the trigger is a press, not a drag.

name: Elliptical visor wipe
description: A scrubbed colour turn between two sections over 720px of scroll. A layer in the next section's ground (for example the ink) is clipped by clip-path ellipse(70% 0% at 50% 0%) and grows to ellipse(70% 100% at 50% 0%) as scroll runs, so a curved lower edge sags down the screen like a visor and ends as full cover. A headline (two lines at the display step, centred, in the opposite ink) is part of the layer in its lower third and is uncovered as the visor passes. Reverse the colours for a light reveal over a dark section. Built with a sticky layer and one CSS variable for the radius: no gradient, no blur. Colour: ground A and ground B (one is the ink), ink flips, accent none.
phone: Ellipse 120% wide; range 540px.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the headline's own 40px rise (the visor uncovers it) and the 72px size (display step). The edge is a hard clip with no gradient and no outline.

name: Ground retones per section
description: The page ground variable and the navigation ink switch to the colour of the section entering the middle line of the viewport, either by a 400ms fade on ease-out (0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) or by a hard cut. Each section declares a ground and an ink from three flat tones: the dealt ground, the surface tone and the ink field (a light or dark field, each used for one section at most), and the section backgrounds themselves are transparent so the page colour shows through. The navigation changes ink at the same instant. Text contrast stays 4.5:1 or better in every state. Colour roles: the dealt ground, the surface tone and one ink field; the accent is never a ground.
phone: Same trigger with the threshold at 55%; with reduced motion use hard cuts.
houseRuleCheck: At most three grounds from the dealt palette (the ground, the surface tone, one ink field), so no colour sprawl; no violet or lavender, flat colours only, never a gradient.

name: Scrubbed ground fade
description: The page ground is a variable blended continuously with scroll between section tones: each section declares a tone, and between its midpoint and the next one's midpoint the ground interpolates in OKLCH over 60-100vh of scroll, so the page breathes from the dealt ground to the surface tone or the ink field. Ink for text and navigation swaps where the ground's lightness crosses 0.6, the point where both inks read at 4.5:1. Inside any section there is no gradient: at every moment the whole page is one flat colour. Three tones only: the dealt ground, the surface tone and one ink field; the accent is never a ground. Colour roles: ground (moving), two inks.
phone: Identical; with reduced motion switch the ground in hard steps at the midpoints.
houseRuleCheck: A white-to-lilac blend is the usual form: lilac and violet are banned, so tones come from the dealt palette; the page is one flat colour at any instant, so it is not a gradient; three tones at most; the optional multiply layer over the pictures is dropped (one grade over every picture).

name: Colour block slides up
description: The next section's flat ground rides up over the current one with a visible straight edge: a full-width sheet (as tall as its content, radius 0) slides over at normal speed, or is scrubbed from translateY(100%) to 0 over 100vh while the section beneath stays pinned. The outgoing section's heading or scene tints with the sweep: a clip-path mask on a second copy of the text (aria-hidden) swaps the ink at the edge's position, so letters change colour exactly as the edge passes them. Hard edge, no gradient, no shadow. Three flat grounds from the dealt palette (the ground, the surface tone, one ink field). Colour roles: flat grounds, two inks; the accent is never a ground.
phone: The same sweep over 90vh; with reduced motion plain stacked sections.
houseRuleCheck: The edge is a straight flat colour change with no shadow and no gradient; at most three colours from the dealt palette, no violet; the sheet is content height, not a full-screen floor.

name: Active title brightens
description: The state style for any list that drives a stepped or pinned scene. A list of 3 to 6 step titles (words, at the sub step, in the display or text face) stacked at the left margin of the scene, 16px apart, or set in a row at the top. Inactive titles sit at 65% ink opacity (4.5:1 or better); the title of the current step goes to 100% over 100ms ease-in (and back over 200ms). Optional: the current title gets a surface-tone chip behind it that fades in, never an underline. Nothing counts or moves; clicking a title jumps to its step. Colour: ink on ground; no accent.
phone: The titles wrap onto two lines under the stage, each target 44px high, the active one at full ink.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: 40% ink (under 4.5:1, now 65%), an accent chip (surface tone) and filled chips on the phone. Step titles are words, never numerals, so there is no index or counter.

name: Stat count-up
description: Figures in two or three filled stat cards (the dealt card style, 300-420px wide, 240-300px high, the surface tone, content left aligned and anchored to the bottom) count from 0 (or from 60-90% of the final value) up to the real value over 1.2-1.8s, ease-out-cubic, once, when the card crosses 70% of the viewport; the cards count together. The numeral is set at the head step in tabular figures, in the display face at tracking -0.02em, with its unit and one line of at most 12 words at the body step saying what it counts. The true final text is in the markup from the start and the card itself is in place from the start. Alternatively one big figure stands inside the sentence that says what it counts. Colour roles: flat ground, card on the surface tone, ink; the accent on a single unit at most.
signature: Each filled card shows a real figure with its unit at the head step that counts up once from 0 to its final value, with one sentence under it saying what it counts and the content anchored to the card's bottom.
phone: Cards one or two across, the numeral at the head step; with reduced motion show the final values at once.
houseRuleCheck: Figures must be real facts with a unit and a meaning, never an index such as 01 or 02 and never a band of figures over one-word labels; cards carry no icon above them and no outline; the cards must not be the only element on the page; designed out: the 72-140px numeral and the entry stagger.

name: Odometer digit roll
description: A real figure the page truly has (a year, a price, a distance, a measure of 2-4 digits), set in the line that says what it counts, at the display or head step in the tabular figures of the page's proportional display face, built from one column per digit. Each column is a clipped window exactly one digit tall (line height 1, overflow hidden) holding the digits 0-9 stacked. On trigger (the section 60 percent in view) each column rolls up by whole rows (one row per step) to its target digit in 1s with expo-out, columns staggered 80ms from the last digit to the first. The true figure is in the HTML and shows in the still and under reduced motion. Ink on ground; no accent. One figure per section, never a band of figures over one-word labels. Phone: the figure at the head step, same roll.
phone: Figure at the head step, same roll.
houseRuleCheck: Clean if used for one real figure in the line that names what it counts (never a stats band); it must never be a 01/02/03 section number or a slide counter, and the digits are tabular figures of the proportional face, not a monospace one. No fill bar beside it.

name: Camera looks with pointer
description: A 3D scene (a room, a shelf of products, an interior, a landscape) whose camera rotates toward or against the pointer: yaw up to 6 degrees and pitch up to 4 degrees (or a sideways offset of 0.3 metres of scene space) with damping lerp 0.08 (floaty) to 0.12 (snappy), returning to centre when the pointer leaves. The scene is the backdrop of the full-screen hero; the hero text (a headline at the display step, two lines at most, and the dealt button) is DOM and stays still, or moves at 0.3 of the camera's parallax for depth. Colour roles: ground = the scene's tone, ink contrasting, accent on the dealt button.
signature: The first screen's backdrop is a 3D scene whose camera yaws up to 6 degrees and pitches up to 4 toward the pointer with a floaty lerp, while the headline stays put.
phone: No pointer, so a gentle auto-sway of 2 degrees on a 10s sine, or device tilt at 3 degrees; with reduced motion a still.
houseRuleCheck: Flat light and fog, no glow and no gradient sky; the hero text sits directly on the scene's calm part with no box.

name: Depth-map pointer parallax
description: A full-bleed hero or scene block where a flat picture gains depth from the pointer. Assets: one photograph (3:2 or 16:10, cover fit) and a cut-out of its main subject (transparent PNG, same framing). The two are stacked layers: the pointer (-1 to 1, eased with lerp 0.06) moves the background picture up to 12px against the pointer and the cut-out up to 36px the other way, with the picture scaled 1.06 to hide the edges. The headline (two lines at the display step) sits on the picture's calm part, of one tone at every width, and never moves. Colour: the picture; type in the ground colour or the ink, whichever reads on the calm part; accent = the dealt button only.
phone: Pointer replaced by a looping drift (8s Lissajous, amplitude 14px) or device tilt where permitted; picture cropped to 100svh.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the greyscale depth map and shader (a cut-out layer does the job) and a headline floating free of the picture's calm part. A modern, designed, generated or product picture, never a documentary photograph; no text box on it.

name: Pointer fluid smear
description: A full-viewport WebGL layer behind the hero runs a fluid simulation (velocity, pressure, curl, dissipation 0.97-0.985, splat radius 0.2-0.35% of the width) in which pointer speed adds velocity and dye. The dye advects and fades in 1.5-3s, and it is thresholded into flat colour regions with crisp edges (smoothstep width 0.01), so the smear reads as liquid paper, never as a soft blend or gradient. Dye uses two tones only: the surface tone and one more palette tone (the ink field, or the accent if the headline stays legible over it), with no colour cycling. The hero headline stays a DOM element at the display step (two lines at most) above the layer, in an ink that holds 4.5:1 on the ground and on the dye. When idle one automatic splat every 4s keeps the scene alive. The system pointer stays visible. Colour roles: flat ground, dye = the surface tone plus one palette tone.
signature: The hero ground reacts to the pointer: moving it drags flat, crisp-edged colour through the ground like liquid paper that fades in 1.5-3s, with the headline unchanged above it.
phone: Touch traces act as the pointer, simulation at 128 resolution, idle splats every 3s; with reduced motion show a still of a smeared frame.
houseRuleCheck: Fluid defaults cycle rainbow colours and blend as gradients: the dye is thresholded to flat regions in two palette tones, never violet; the difference blend over the headline is dropped; pair only with a calm hero because it is heavy.

name: Pointer image trail
description: On a flat ground the pointer leaves pictures behind it. Each time the pointer has travelled about one sixteenth of the viewport width (90px at 1440) a new picture is placed centred on it: 150-240px on its long side, in the dealt corner, with a random tilt of up to 6 degrees, taken in turn from a set of six pictures that appear nowhere else on the page. A picture starts at 0.8 scale and 0 opacity and reaches 1 in 200ms (expo-out) and stays while the pointer moves; once the pointer has rested 350ms the pictures leave one by one, oldest first, shrinking to 0.2 and fading over 0.8-1.2s. No more than 6 are alive at once and the newest is on top. The native cursor stays. The stage is one section (or the hero) with a headline at the display step (2-4 words, two lines at most, ink) and the dealt button on the ground; at rest no picture lies under the headline, and while the pointer moves the pictures pass under it so it stays readable. The stage is finished at rest (headline and button only), so nothing arrives on load. The pictures are modern, well lit stills or cut-outs in the page's one grade, never documentary photographs; ground and ink are flat and the accent is used only on the action. Phone: no pointer, so a tap drops the next picture at the finger (100px), four alive at most, each fading after 1.2s.
phone: No pointer: a tap drops a 100px picture at the finger, four alive at most.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. The pictures are the page's own six, each shown nowhere else, in one grade and never documentary; they pass under the headline only in motion, so no words sit on a photograph at rest and no box or caption touches one. The native cursor stays (no custom cursor). Nothing arrives on load.

name: Pill label follows cursor
description: A label follows the pointer over targets (picture cards, tiles, list rows): a filled block 32px tall with 14px side padding in the dealt button's corner, the accent fill with accent-ink letters at the body step in the dealt button's weight, holding one or two words in sentence case that name what a click does (Open, Play, Read the story). It trails the pointer about 16px to the right and below it, eased with a 0.12 lerp so it lags by a few frames, and it exists only over a target. On entering a target it grows from 0.7 scale and 0 opacity to 1 in 300ms on the house curve with no overshoot, while the native pointer stays visible beside it; on leaving it shrinks back in 200ms. Within 140px of the right or bottom edge it flips to the left or above the pointer so it never leaves the viewport. When the pointer moves from one target type to another the words change by a short mask roll (180ms). Ground and ink are the page's own; only the label takes the accent. Phone: no cursor, so each target carries its own visible dealt button instead.
phone: No cursor; every target shows its own visible dealt button.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. A companion label, not a cursor: the system pointer always stays and nothing overshoots. It is a filled block with sentence-case words at 16px, not a caption box on a photograph, and it takes the dealt button's corner so the page keeps one button shape. Hidden on touch, where each target shows its own dealt button.

name: Pointer lens warp
description: A pointer lens on a full-bleed photograph, or on a block inside the page margins. A shader on the picture plane bulges the image inside a 180px radius (at 1440) around the eased pointer (lerp 0.1): the uv is pushed away from the pointer by 0.18 x (1 - smoothstep(0, radius, distance)), which magnifies the centre smoothly with no colour fringe. The lens grows from 0 to full radius in 400ms on entering the block and back in 400ms on leaving. The lens is invisible as a shape: no rim, no highlight. The headline (two lines at the display step) stands on the picture's calm part or on the ground above it and never moves. Colour: the picture only.
phone: A touch-drag moves the lens; at rest the lens drifts along a slow path every 8s; radius 120px.
houseRuleCheck: No rim or glass highlight: a pure distortion, not a glass object. Words sit only on the picture's calm part or on the ground.

name: Paint trail reveal
description: A pointer-painted reveal on a large photograph. Two treatments of the same image are stacked in a canvas: a base (full colour) and an alternate (the surface tone with a halftone dot pattern in the ink, cell 16px, dot size from luminance). The pointer paints a brush (radius 0.04 of the canvas width) into a 512x512 offscreen buffer that fades x0.97 per frame, so the trail shows about 2s of path. The mix between the treatments follows the buffer: the picture turns to the surface tone and halftone where the pointer has passed and heals as the trail decays. The block fills the content width inside the page margins at about 700px high with the dealt corner, or is a full-bleed hero; a two-line headline at the display step sits on the plain ground above or beside it, not on the picture. Colour: ground and ink as dealt, no accent.
phone: A touch-drag paints; at rest a short brush path crosses the picture once to show it works.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the flat ink duotone base (a full-colour base keeps the one picture grade) and the 96px headline (display step). Halftone is a texture of dots, not a drawn illustration; text stays off the picture.

name: Hover preview follows
description: A list of five rows (one picture each), each with a name at the head step starting at the left margin and a short descriptor aligned right at the body step, rows 120-160px tall on the ground, no divider rules (separation by space and by the row's own fill on hover). Hovering a row fades in a preview picture 280-320px wide (4:5 or 3:2, dealt corner) over 0.5s (power2-out) which follows the pointer with a spring (stiffness about 170, damping 26, or a 0.12 lerp), offset 24px to its right and tilting up to 4 degrees with pointer speed. The row takes the ink fill with ground-coloured letters in 180ms; the other rows stay. Leaving fades the preview out in 0.5s. One picture per row. Phone: no hover, so a tap opens the row as an accordion with its picture at full width, 4:3, one open at a time.
phone: Tap opens the row as an accordion with a full-width 4:3 picture.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. No hairline dividers between rows; the filled row is the row's own fill; names start at the left margin so rows are not empty on the left; the preview is a picture in the dealt corner with no box or caption on it.

name: Pointer repel field
description: A stage one section after the hero, 100svh tall on a flat ground, holds six picture tiles (160-220px on the long side, dealt corner) scattered in a loose arrangement with 8-20 percent jitter, each picture shown nowhere else on the page. A pointer within 220px of a tile pushes it away along the line from the pointer (force falling off with the square of the distance, up to 90px) and rotates it up to 15 degrees; pointer speed scales the push. When the pointer leaves, each tile eases home by 5 percent of its remaining offset per frame, about 600ms. A heading at the head step (2-4 words, two lines at most) sits centred above the tiles in z-order, and no tile rests on it. There is no fluid trail. Phone: no pointer, so tiles drift away from a touch while the finger is down and otherwise float 6px on a slow sine.
phone: Tiles drift away from a held touch, otherwise float 6px.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Tiles are the page's own pictures, each shown once; no decorative drawn discs; the heading is plain type without a box and nothing rests on it.

name: Tilt toward pointer
description: One card or picture (a filled card in the dealt style, or a single large picture) rotates in perspective (perspective 900-1200px) toward the pointer: rotateX and rotateY up to 6-10 degrees at a strength of about 0.2 of the normalised pointer offset, returning on leave by a critically damped spring (stiffness 170, damping 26, no overshoot) or a 500ms ease-out. For a card 360-480px wide the picture inside counter-translates 8-14px for depth. No shine overlay and no shadow. Use it on one or two key objects per page, not on every card. Colour roles: none.
phone: Not on touch; device orientation at 4 degrees is optional and off by default; with reduced motion none.
houseRuleCheck: No glare or shine gradient and no moving shadow: the rotation alone carries it. Designed out: tilting a disc or a text block, and the 3D-model variant (the 3D patterns own that).

name: Pointer lights the text
description: A statement block where the pointer lights the words. A statement of 12 to 20 words at 36px (the sub step), three lines at most, 900px wide at most, each word in its own span (aria-label on the parent). At rest every word sits at 65% ink opacity, already readable at 4.5:1. As the pointer moves each word's opacity eases (120ms) to 65% + 35% x (1 - clamp(distance / 220px)), distance taken from the pointer to the word's centre, so words near the pointer read at full ink while the rest stay dimmer; leaving the block returns all to 65% in 500ms. There is no lamp, glow or light shape: only the words change. Colour: ground flat, ink; accent none.
phone: No pointer: the words light by distance from a line at 45% of the viewport height as the block scrolls through it; text at 24px on four lines.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: 36-48px over 5 lines (a paragraph statement is 36px or less on three lines) and the 45% rest opacity (under 4.5:1, now 65%). No lamp shape and no glow: per-word opacity does the lighting.

name: Leaf shadow sway
description: A ground texture for one calm section (a quote, values or story block) as tall as its content. A fragment shader fills the section with dappled light and shadow: domain-warped noise thresholded with a smoothstep between 0.42 and 0.5 so the patches read as leaf-shaped shadows, in the ink at 8 to 12% opacity over the section's own ground. The pattern sways on time (offset sin(t x 0.3) x 12px on a slow 20s drift) and is nudged by the pointer through a spring (stiffness 40, damping 8, up to 20px). The layer is there from the first frame and moves up 77px against the page while the section passes. Text and cards above are flat and opaque, in front of the texture. Colour: ground as dealt, patches = the ink at low opacity, accent none.
phone: The pointer is replaced by a 14s autonomous drift; half resolution; paused when off screen.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the 100vh section (content height), the texture fading in on view (it is there at once) and a warm paper ground (the dealt ground). An ambient texture, not a UI drop shadow: every card and text block stays flat and patch edges stay crisp, so no soft glow.

name: Glitch slice handover
description: A first-scroll handover on a hero photograph. The hero shows one photograph or cut-out plane (centred, about 620px tall) on a flat ground. Over the first 400px of scroll (scrubbed, no pin) the plane breaks into 10 to 16 horizontal slices (strips of the same texture, 40 to 62px high). The slices offset sideways by random distances (30 to 160px) with a 30ms stagger, then slide out left and right while the next section's ground wipes in. The rest state is clean. Colour: the picture carries the colour, ground flat, ink for text.
phone: 8 slices, offsets up to 60px; range 200px.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the timed 900ms play-out (the slices follow the scroll). No wireframe or thin lines behind the picture and no flicker: the slices move once and leave. The hero still fills the first screen alone.

name: Glyph fragments flip in
description: A hover move on one large word or link (the closing line, a section link). The word is set at the display step, one or two lines. Each letter is cut into 3 or 4 horizontal strips (the DOM letter cloned once per strip and clipped with clip-path inset so each shows one band). On hover or focus the strips turn through a full rotateX turn (perspective 800px), the strips of one letter 20ms apart and letters 25ms apart, 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), about 1.1s in all; while turning the strips are tinted with the accent and the tint settles to the ink over 400ms after the last strip lands, so at rest it is one plain word. Plays once per hover. Set aria-label on the parent and hide the strips from screen readers.
phone: Plays once on tap; 2 strips per letter; the word at the display step.
houseRuleCheck: Recast: the title build on load is dropped (the dealt entrance decides arrival); the same strip flip runs on hover and press. The tint is transient, not a styled accent word; nothing glows and nothing is left at rest.

name: Halftone shader treatment
description: One picture (the hero's, or one section's) is rendered by a fragment shader as a halftone in exactly two colours from the palette: ink dots on the ground, or ground dots on the accent where that is the screen's one use of the accent. The grid has 4-8px cells at 45 degrees and the dot radius follows the picture's luminance; a scan-line variant uses 3px lines of varying thickness. The treatment is persistent on that one picture and the first frame is the finished halftone (nothing reveals on load). On press and hold the dots swell and go gooey (metaball blend 0.58, contrast 1.5, wave amplitude doubled) and relax over 600ms on release. No type sits on the halftone: the headline stands on the ground beside or under it, in ink. Every other picture on the page keeps the page's one grade. Phone: 6px cells, press effect by touch.
phone: 6px cells, press effect by touch.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Two flat colours, no smooth tones: the impression of tone comes from dot size, not from a gradient. No box and no type over the picture; it is a print treatment of one modern photograph, not a grey filter, and it is the only treated picture.

name: Angled image wipe
description: A gallery of three cards in the dealt card style, each with two pictures (for example the product, then the same product in use). The picture runs to the card's edges at the top; the card's title (sub step) and one line of 16px text stand under it in the card's fill. The two pictures are stacked (or mixed in a shader) and the top one is wiped through an edge angled at 30 degrees, progress 0 to 1 over 700ms cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1), on hover (desktop) or when the card passes the middle of the viewport (touch); the picture scales 1.04 on hover. CSS version: two stacked images, the top one clipped by clip-path polygon(0 0, X% 0, calc(X% - 12%) 100%, 0 100%) with X animated from 0 to 112. Cards about 440x560. Colour: card = the surface tone, ink for text.
phone: The wipe plays once when the card is 60% in view; no hover state.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the 16px radius and tint fill (the dealt corner and card fill) and the extra scroll parallax. Text sits in the card's fill under the picture, never over it; each of the six pictures appears once.

name: Zoomable flat map
description: A map block across the content width inside the page margins, about 640px high, with the dealt corner. The map is real map data styled in the page's tones: land = the surface tone, water = the ground, roads = the ground tone (3px or wider), labels = the ink (16px, sentence case). 8 to 12 pins are ink dots (14px) and the open one takes the accent; a pin opens a card in the dealt card style (surface fill, 260px wide, a title at the lead step and one line of 16px text) on hover or tap, growing from scale 0 to 1 at the pin point in 250ms on the dealt curve, never with an overshoot, and shrinking back in 200ms on leave. Controls: zoom in and zoom out buttons, 48px squares in the dealt button's fill and corner with the typeface's plus and minus, at the lower right 24px in; wheel zoom only with ctrl or cmd held so the page still scrolls; a three-stop zoom (region, city, street) and an idle auto-fly between pins every 6s until the visitor touches the map. The data licence's one-line attribution sits in the corner at 13px.
phone: Block the full width minus the page margins, 70svh high; two-finger pan and zoom (one finger scrolls the page); pins open the card as a bottom sheet; buttons 44px.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: four map colours (ground, surface tone and ink only), accent pins, round zoom buttons and 12-14px small text. Pins are dots, not icons; the attribution is one short line, not a credit wall; no gradient, no outline.

name: Veil dissolves on load
description: A loading state for a 3D canvas: until the model has loaded, the canvas waits on a flat veil in the page ground colour (that is loading, not a reveal). When loading finishes the veil does not fade as a sheet: it dissolves through an ordered 4x4 dither threshold in a fragment shader (or a canvas), cells of 4px dropping out in a noisy order across 1s (inOutCubic on the threshold), so the scene appears through shrinking dots of ground and then clears. The page's own first screen (headline, sentence, action) is HTML around the canvas and readable from the first frame, and arrives with the dealt entrance; only the canvas waits. Colour: veil = page ground, scene = its own colours; no accent.
phone: Cells 6px, 0.8s, DPR 1.
houseRuleCheck: Covers only the canvas, never the page's words, and never holds the first screen; one flat ground colour dissolved by a dither threshold, no gradient, no pulse.

name: Noise dissolve reveal
description: A picture swap through a noise dissolve, on a large photograph inside the page margins (the dealt corner) or a full-bleed block. Two photographs are drawn by a shader with a progress value 0 to 1 over 1.6s (cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)), started by a press on the dealt second-action link or by the arrow keys. A noise field (x, y and a fixed seed) is compared with the progress: pixels below the threshold show the next photograph, pixels above show the current one. At the leading edge a band about 60px wide shows the next photograph as halftone dots (cell 10px, dot radius shrinking toward the unrevealed side). The first photograph is there from the first frame. Colour: the photographs carry the colour; ground as dealt.
phone: Same shader at DPR 1 over 1.2s; or a CSS mask-image with a bitmap noise PNG whose mask-position animates.
houseRuleCheck: Recast: the one-shot reveal on load or on entering view is dropped (the dealt entrance decides arrival); it is a picture swap on a press. The brightness pulse is removed. Halftone is a texture of dots, not a drawn illustration.

name: Drifting noise ground
description: A fragment shader (fractal noise, 4-5 octaves, flow speed 0.02-0.05 of the noise scale per second) drifts slowly behind the hero (100svh) as smoke or cloud sheets in the dealt ground and the surface tone (a third band in the ink field if the page has one). It is posterised into 4-6 flat bands with crisp edges (smoothstep width 0.01), so it reads as layered paper rather than a soft glow. The headline is DOM text on top at the display step (two lines at most), with the dealt button beneath. Render at 50% resolution and upscale; pause when hidden; a static frame under reduced motion and data saver. Colour roles: ground = the darkest band, the surface tone as the lighter bands, ink contrasting, the accent only on the dealt button.
signature: The hero ground is a slowly drifting field of crisp-edged flat bands (layered paper, not a soft glow) in the ground and surface tones, with the headline on top.
phone: Resolution 35%, speed halved; with reduced motion one still frame.
houseRuleCheck: It often adds faint arcs and ramp discs: dropped as drawn shapes. Smooth blends read as gradients, so the noise is quantised to flat colour bands; it stays behind the hero only, with no darkening per chapter.

name: Velocity bend
description: Pictures are WebGL planes aligned with their DOM boxes (4:5, about 380x475, in a 3-column gallery or a vertical list). A shader offsets the vertices by scroll velocity: planes bend (a sine curve up to 40px at top speed), relaxing by a 0.08 lerp to flat within 400ms when scrolling stops. Scroll is smoothed (lerp 0.1) so velocity is continuous. Planes use cover-fit textures, and the captions stay DOM text beneath each picture at the body step. On hover a plane scales 1.04 and a ripple follows the pointer for 600ms. Colour roles: flat ground, the pictures bring the colour, ink for captions. Variant: one fixed canvas draws every picture of the page as such a plane on its hidden DOM box (cover fit, the dealt corner in the shader, a parallax of plus or minus 8% of its height by scroll position, at most 8 planes active), all text staying real DOM, with plain images as the fallback when the frame rate drops.
phone: Bend at 40%, no hover; with reduced motion render plain DOM images.
houseRuleCheck: No colour split, no glow and no blur on the pictures (never blurred, one grade); pictures must not be documentary photographs; designed out: the up-to-2px blur at speed.

name: Planes drift, photo covers
description: A hero made of drifting picture planes. 5 image planes (180 to 420px wide, photographs or generated pictures with soft crops) hang in a field at different depths around a centred two-line title at the display step. During the first 360px of scroll (scrubbed, no pin) the planes drift upward at depth-dependent speeds (0.4x to 1.6x of the scroll) while the title lifts and fades; at 360px the first full-bleed photograph of the next section (cover fit, 100vw by 90vh, the dealt corner on its top corners) slides up over them as a sheet, so the planes are covered rather than scrolled away. Colour: ground flat, the planes carry the colour, the title in ink.
phone: 4 planes at 120 to 260px; title at the display step; range 280px.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: 8 to 12 planes (5 planes plus the cover photograph make the 6 pictures a page may have) and the 120px three-word title (two lines, display step). The hero fills the first screen alone (the cover sheet appears only on scroll); no text boxes on the planes.

name: Cinematic post pass
description: One full-screen canvas in the hero or in one stage section (never the whole page) draws one picture of the page through a shader. The shader applies the page's one grade and a fine grain: contrast 1.05-1.1, saturation 0.9-1.1, one slight temperature push (warm or cool, as the sheet deals) with the darkest tones lifted a little; then film grain at 3-6 percent amplitude, re-seeded 24 times a second (or a 4x4 ordered dither at 1.5 percent). There is no channel split, no vignette, no bloom and no glow. The canvas runs at a pixel ratio capped at 1.5 and drops to grain only below 40fps. All type over the stage is HTML outside the canvas, set on the picture's calm part in one tone, so letters stay crisp. The picture is a modern, well lit photograph or cut-out, never documentary and never greyed. The first frame is the finished graded picture; the grade does not fade in. Ground and ink come from the page; the accent stays on the action. Phone: grain and grade stay, pixel ratio 1.
phone: Grain and grade only, pixel ratio 1.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Grade and grain only: a vignette (a gradient), bloom (a glow), a red-blue lens split and a milky fog are all left out, and the grade is the page's one grade, never a grey filter. No glass, no overlay boxes, nothing laid over the picture but its own grain.

name: Shader scene transition
description: Three or four full-screen scenes (photographs rendered to textures) blend through a fragment shader driven by a progress value 0-1: a noise-threshold dissolve, a liquid warp or a depth-mask wipe, with no colour split. The scenes sit on a held stage of about one screen each (three screens of scroll at most): when the scroll crosses a scene's midpoint the blend plays over 1.0-1.4s as a timed step, and a text Next control (the dealt second-action style) and the arrow keys do the same; the wheel itself is never captured. Each scene is full-bleed with a headline at the head step (two lines at most) at the bottom-left and one body-step link, set on the calm part of the photograph with no box; the outgoing text fades over 300ms and the incoming text rises after 600ms. Headline in the ground colour or the ink, whichever reads on each scene. Colour roles: scenes carry their own colour, accent none.
phone: Native scroll crosses the same midpoints, shader resolution 0.75, headline at the head step; with reduced motion use a 300ms crossfade.
houseRuleCheck: The frost variant looks like glass and is dropped; use dissolve, liquid or depth-mask only, no gradient overlay between scenes, no colour split and no wheel capture; the hold is cut to three screens.

name: Reel tilts up on hover
description: A media card whose reel plays on hover. A card in the dealt card style (440x340) with the poster still (the reel's first frame) running to the card's edges at the top (440x240) and a title at the sub step with one line of 16px text in the fill below. The reel (a video clip) sits in the picture area and on hover tilts up from rotateX(38deg) scale(0.95) opacity 0 to rotateX(0) scale(1) opacity 1, perspective 1000px, transform-origin at the bottom edge, 600ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), playing from the start; leaving reverses it over 350ms and pauses. Use three cards. Colour: card = the surface tone, ink for the title, accent for at most one link.
phone: No hover: the reel tilts up and plays once when the card is 60% in view, one card at a time.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: a picture frame inset in the card (the picture runs to the card's edges) and the 20px radius (the dealt corner). No text boxes on the reel; the card is a fill.

name: Arrow exits and re-enters
description: A button built around one swapped arrow. It is 52px tall in the dealt corner, filled with the ink (on a dark page the surface tone), with the label at the body step in the ground colour at the left (22px padding) and, at the right, a 24px clipped window holding a typeset arrow glyph in the accent. On hover the arrow slides out of the window to the right (100 percent of the window, 350ms expo-out) while a copy slides in from the left through the same window, and the label nudges 6px to follow. The width is fixed from the start so nothing around moves. On a phone there is no hover, so the swap runs on press.
signature: On hover the arrow leaves the button to the right while an identical one enters from the left through the same 24px window and the label nudges 6px, so the button is never a still rectangle.
phone: No hover: the swap runs on press; the button keeps its width and is 52px tall.
houseRuleCheck: Solid fill, no outline, no shadow; the arrow is a typeset glyph and its window has no fill of its own. One button design on the page: the second action is the label alone with the same arrow swap.

name: Arrow nudges diagonally
description: The micro-motion on a button or link that ends in an arrow (the typeface's own arrow glyph, not an icon set). On hover or focus the arrow translates up and right by 3px (translate(3px, -3px), 200ms ease-out) and returns on leave; the label stays still. It adds to the dealt button's own hover and never replaces it, and it works on any button or text link that ends in an arrow, 44px or taller. Keep the arrow at 0.9em. Colour: as the button; nothing else.
phone: Plays on tap down; no persistent hover state.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the pattern's own fill shift (the dealt button's hover decides the fill). No outline.

name: Caption foot rises
description: A row of three photo cards at 1440, each a third of the content width less the gaps (about 416px wide at 4:5), 24px apart, in the dealt corner, on the surface tone. At rest the photograph (the one dealt grade) fills the card down to a 64px foot holding a one-line title at the lead step and, at the right, a typeset arrow glyph in the accent. On hover the foot grows by 130px (450ms expo-out) while the picture slides up inside the card by the same amount, so the foot never covers the photograph; after 120ms a two-line paragraph at the body step fades in and the arrow turns to the diagonal. Colour roles: card on the surface tone, ink text, accent only on the arrow. The row arrives with the dealt entrance. On a phone the cards go one per row at the page width, the foot is permanently open with the paragraph visible, and no animation runs.
signature: On hover the 64px caption foot grows to about 194px while the photograph slides up inside the card by the same amount, so the caption never covers the picture.
phone: One card per row, foot permanently open with the paragraph shown; no hover motion.
houseRuleCheck: A photograph card with no box on it: the foot is the card's own part and the picture moves up as it rises. Paragraph at 16px. One surface tone, the dealt corner, no outline, no shadow. Use it in one section so the page is not only cards.

name: Pill appears around
description: Hover or focus on a nav word makes a solid block appear behind it: 36-44px tall with 10px 18px padding in the dealt corner, filled with the surface tone (or the accent with accent-ink letters), opacity 0 to 1 and scale 0.9 to 1 in 150-250ms. The current page keeps its block and its label goes up one loaded weight without reflow (the width is reserved by a hidden copy in the heavier weight). A shared block that glides from item to item (300ms, expo-out) can replace per-item blocks. Use it where the dealt navigation names no hover of its own; the dealt button is never given it. Phone: no hover; the current item keeps the block.
phone: No hover; the current item keeps the pill.
houseRuleCheck: Clean when solid: no ring, outline or glow; the block is a flat fill in the dealt corner, the surface tone or the accent, never an added tint.

name: Button fill inverts
description: A hover for the dealt button; its size, corner, label size and padding stay exactly as dealt, and at rest it keeps its dealt fill with no outline. On hover the fill and the label colour swap places at once (a button filled with the ink turns ground-coloured with ink letters; a soft-filled button turns solid ink with ground letters), a plain swap over 200-240ms on ease-out (0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) with nothing travelling (a fill that sweeps across is a different pattern). Pressed: scale 0.98 for 90ms. Keyboard focus shows the hover state plus a 3px focus ring in the accent offset by 3px. Colour roles: ground and ink swap; the accent appears only in the focus ring.
signature: On hover the whole button flips fill and label colour at once (200-240ms, nothing travels or sweeps), and keyboard focus adds a 3px accent ring set 3px off the button.
phone: No hover on touch: the pressed state shows the swapped colours for 150ms; the dealt button keeps its dealt touch size.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the usual outlined rest state and the pattern's own button size, corner and label. When the dealt button already names its own hover, that one wins and this swap goes on the second action only.

name: Fill sweeps across
description: On hover a fill the size of the element sweeps across it. Use it on nav links (a 36px fill) and list rows; the dealt button keeps its own hover and is never given this one. The fill (the accent, or the ink) in the dealt corner, optionally skewed 8-12 degrees so its leading edge is diagonal, enters from the left (translateX -101 percent to 0) in 525ms on cubic-bezier 0.625, 0.05, 0, 1, and the label's colour flips to the ground colour (accent-ink on the accent) in step: the label has two copies, one rolling up out of a mask and the other rolling in from below. On leave the fill exits to the right (0 to 101 percent), so the motion always travels left to right. Keyboard focus does the same. Phone: no hover; the pressed state fills in 250ms from the touch side.
phone: No hover; press fills in 250ms.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Flat fill in the dealt corner, no gradient edge, no outline, no shadow; it is a hover state for links and rows, not a second button design.

name: One house easing
description: One timing pair is defined once as variables on the root and used for every hover, focus, open, close and small move on the page (the dealt entrance keeps its own timing): a single strong ease-out such as cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) and a single duration chosen per site (240, 400 or 560ms). Large moves may use the same curve at 1.6x the duration. No linear, no browser default ease, no second curve. The choice sets the character: a quick-out at 240ms feels crisp and technical, a long out at 560ms feels soft and expensive. Scroll-linked smoothing and library tweens read the same numbers so everything on the page moves as one family. Colour roles: none. It is invisible, but it is the difference between a page that is built and a page that is assembled.
phone: Same tokens with durations at 0.8x; hover timings are not needed on touch, press and open timings keep the curve.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict. It is a token, not an effect, so it can sit under every other motion pattern.

name: Indent with dot
description: For rows or links in a list (a menu sheet, a project list, a footer link list) set at the lead step or larger (never under 16px) with 14-20px between rows. On hover or keyboard focus the label moves right by about 0.5em (about 40px at the head step, 12-20px at the lead step) over 400-500ms on the house ease-out (no overshoot) while a 10-16px dot in the accent scales from 0 to 1 in the space it leaves at the left. The ink does not change. The other rows stay still or dim to 0.6 (dealt per page, never lower, so every row keeps 4.5:1). On leave it reverses in 300ms. The dot is a plain CSS disc, never an icon. Rows are separated by space alone, with no rules and no boxes. Phone: there is no hover, so the row nearest the middle of the viewport (or the tapped row) shows the dot and the indent and the others rest.
phone: No hover: the row nearest the viewport middle, or the tapped one, shows the dot and indent.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. The dot is a CSS disc used as a state mark, not a drawn shape or an icon; rows are separated by space, never by hairline dividers, and are not boxed. The accent appears only on the dot.

name: Label roll-up
description: The label of the navigation links (and of the dealt button where its design names no hover of its own) sits in an overflow-hidden slot one line high (line-height 1.2). An identical twin of the label waits directly beneath. On hover both move up 100% over 380-480ms on ease-out (0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), so the label leaves through the top while its twin enters from below into the same place. The twin has the same colour, or the accent on a text link. The width and height of the control never change. Optional: a typed arrow glyph beside the label turns 45 degrees. Keyboard focus triggers the same roll. Label size, case and weight stay as dealt. Use it on the navigation links and that one button only, never on body text links. Colour roles: ground, ink; the accent only for the twin on a text link.
signature: On hover the label slides out through the top of its one-line slot while an identical copy rises into the same place from below (380-480ms), and the control's box does not move.
phone: No hover on touch: play the roll on press (240ms); the dealt button keeps its touch size; with reduced motion swap the label instantly.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict; the arrow is a typed glyph, not a drawn icon. Designed out: its own button size and the button growing 4% wider (the dealt width is fixed).

name: Lift on hover
description: A small lift for the dealt button's second action and for any button the dealt design leaves still. On hover the button rises 3px (translateY, 200ms ease-out) and on press it returns to 0 in 120ms; its shape, size, corner, fill and label do not change. On a phone it runs on the active press state only. It is the plain default: use it only when another special treatment already carries the page.
