houseRuleCheck: The receipt cue comes from the stepped motion only: no monospace type, no dotted or hairline rules between lines (use spacing), no drawn torn edge, no shadow, one surface tone. The bar is a flat filled shape, not an outlined box. Scroll-driven, so the dealt entrance is not overridden.

name: Untilt settle
description: A row or grid of 3-4 photograph tiles (each 4:5, about 400x500 at 1440, the dealt corner, 24px gaps) arrives tilted and settles flat. As each tile crosses from 90% to 55% of the viewport height its rotateZ runs from 5.7deg to 0 (alternate the sign so neighbours lean opposite ways) and its scale from 1.02 to 1.0, transform-origin at the bottom centre, scrubbed with 0.3s smoothing. The end state is dead flat so the grid reads as aligned and calm; photographs stay sharp, with no blur and no opacity change. Tiles are photographs only, never several fills; ground as dealt. The section clips overflow because a tilted tile pokes out by about 25px, and the tiles keep the page margins at rest. Phone: single column, tilt 3.5deg, one tile per screen.
phone: Single column inside the page margins; tilt 3.5deg, scale 1.02 to 1.0, one tile per screen; reduced motion: no tilt.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict. Scroll-linked, so the dealt entrance stands. No frames, shadows or overlays on the photographs, one grade over all of them, never outlined.

name: Camera rides to the next room
description: One fixed full-viewport WebGL canvas holds 3-5 modelled rooms or objects (a product on a plinth, a building volume, a stage set), each standing for one section and laid out along a spline. A nav link or a next control triggers a camera ride along a Catmull-Rom curve from room to room (1.8s, ease-in-out cubic, 4% field-of-view breathe at mid-flight). A flat ground-colour transition plane takes the progress: the outgoing DOM text fades in the first 30%, the incoming text rises through a mask in the last 30%. Text is DOM over the canvas: a headline at the display step, a lead-step sub and at most the dealt button. Materials are flat or unlit (no gradient, no soft shadow); the fog is the page ground colour; ink is the text and the accent sits on one object per room. Keep the URL in sync (history pushState) so rooms are deep links. The first screen is the first room alone.
phone: Same camera path with the canvas DPR capped at 1.5; text at the head step bottom-aligned, the dealt button full width; without WebGL, reduced motion or data saver, swap to a crossfade between static renders of each room.
houseRuleCheck: Rooms must be modelled objects that stand for the subject, not floating abstract primitives or drawn shapes; flat shading only (no gradient), no shadows at rest, no glass materials. It needs real 3D models the page must supply or build itself.

name: Image flies between pages
description: An index of 6-12 project thumbnails (3:2, about 420x280 at 1440, the dealt corner, 24px gaps) leads to detail pages. On click the thumbnail's rectangle is measured, the rest of the grid fades out in 250ms, and the same image element animates (FLIP, or the view-transitions API) to the detail hero frame (full width inside the page margins, about 680px tall under the nav) in 0.9s ease-in-out-expo. During the flight the picture drifts inside its frame (translateY 8% to 0) so it seems to slide within a window. After landing, the title (display step) and the body arrive with the dealt entrance. Back reverses the flight. Ground and ink as dealt.
phone: Thumbnails in one column; the flight lands in a full-width 4:3 frame; reduced motion: crossfade.
houseRuleCheck: No colour split on the flying picture (RGB ghosts are a house no); nothing is outlined or shadowed; use modern designed or generated imagery, never documentary photographs.

name: Iris mask reveal
description: A full-screen view opens through a circular clip: the menu, or a view of the page's own content. The view sits above the page in a fixed layer on its own opaque ground and is revealed by clip-path circle(0 at X Y) to circle(150% at X Y) over 900ms cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1), where X Y is the click point (or the corner of the menu button). It closes by the same circle shrinking back to the click point over 700ms. The circle has no border and no noise edge. Both views keep their own grounds; the page behind keeps its scroll place; focus moves into the view and back, and Esc closes it. Under reduced motion crossfade over 300ms.
phone: Origin at the tap point; 800ms.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the noise-edge variant (a drawn wobble). A mask between two full views with no outline and no gradient edge; it opens on a click and is never a gate held before the page.

name: Route swap crossfade
description: Dialogs and, on a site with several pages, internal navigation swap content with a crossfade: the outgoing content fades to 0 over 240-320ms while the incoming fades up from 0 over 320-480ms, overlapping by about 100ms; the page returns to the top, and the navigation stays in place. A page-swap script or the browser's view-transition support does the work, with a plain page load as the fallback. A dialog (the menu panel, Image credits) opens with the same fade plus a 0.98 to 1 scale over 280ms on a flat ink backdrop at 40%. Total under 700ms so it never feels like waiting. Colour roles: none.
phone: Same swap at 200ms; with reduced motion switch instantly.
houseRuleCheck: The backdrop is a flat ink tone, never a blurred glass layer. Designed out: the sound toggle and the rise on the incoming page (arrival belongs to the dealt entrance).

name: Tile grows into a drawer
description: A grid of six filled tiles in the surface tone (3 across, each about 440x300 at 1440, the dealt corner, 24px gaps), each holding a short title at the sub step and one line. On click the tile itself animates width, height and position (FLIP, 1.5s, ease-in-out-expo) into a right-hand drawer 720px wide by the full viewport height; the other tiles drop to 40% brightness through a flat black scrim (no blur). The tile's fill becomes the drawer's fill, so the colour visibly grows into the panel. After the tile has covered 70% of its path the drawer's content arrives with the dealt entrance: the title (head step), one short paragraph (body step), one photograph and the dealt button. Close reverses; the URL keeps the open state.
phone: The tile grows to a full-screen sheet from its own position (1.1s); the close control is the dealt button at its phone height at the bottom inside the safe area; reduced motion: crossfade.
houseRuleCheck: No box in a box: drawer content sits directly on the drawer's fill with no inner cards; separation from the page is the scrim, not a shadow or outline; the scrim is flat, not glass; one surface tone for the tiles, never a wall of tiles in several fills.

name: Wipe layer
description: Between the page and the pages it links to (a second page, or the full-screen menu sheet), never on the first load, a flat full-screen layer in the ink field covers the screen. It scales on Y from the bottom (origin bottom, 0 to 1 in 500-800ms, cubic-bezier 0.76, 0, 0.2, 1), holds 150ms while the route swaps, then leaves upward (origin top, 1 to 0 in 500-700ms). While it moves the outgoing page shifts up 100px; the new page is already in place under the layer with its finished first screen (the dealt entrance decides what moves in it). A strip variant uses 4-6 vertical bars staggered 60ms across the width instead of one layer. The layer carries nothing, or one centred word at the head step in the ground colour naming the destination. Total 1.2-1.6s; skipped on back navigation and under reduced motion. Phone: the same, timings 15 percent shorter, strips reduced to 3.
phone: Same wipe, 15 percent shorter, three strips.
houseRuleCheck: Clean when flat: the layer is one flat colour with a hard edge, no gradient, no diagonal pattern, no hairlines. It never runs on the first load (no preloader), and the new page's first frame is its finished first screen.

name: Circle swap with a turn
description: A stepped slide where each slide is a circular photograph crop (about 560px across at 1440, sitting right of centre) with its caption on the left: a title at the head step and a one-line sub (lead step, 40 characters wide at most). A step comes from an arrow key, a click on the dealt button or a swipe, never from a timer. The outgoing circle turns to -15deg while shrinking to scale 0.3 and fading as it slides 80px up and out (0.8s); the incoming circle rises from 80px below, turns from 15deg to 0 and grows from 0.3 to 1 (0.9s, ease-out-expo), overlapping by 0.3s. Because the picture rotates inside its circle, the turn reads clearly. Caption lines rise through masks 60ms apart. The ground stays one flat tone throughout, ink as dealt, accent only on the dealt button. No dots, no counter.
phone: Circle 78vw centred above its caption; swipe steps; turn 10deg; reduced motion: crossfade.
houseRuleCheck: A circular photo crop is a mask, not a drawn shape; no ring outline around it, no slide counter or numbered dots; slides move only by the visitor's hand, never on a timer.

name: Full-bleed shrinks to frame
description: A pinned stage after the hero (100svh, 1.2-2 viewport heights of scroll). A full-screen picture at 1440 x 900 scales down, by transform or clip and never by layout, to a centred frame 34-42 percent of the width (about 520 x 640 portrait or 640 x 400 landscape) while its radius grows from 0 to the dealt corner. In the same scroll the ground behind turns from the picture's edge tone to the page ground (a cross-fade of two flat colours, not a gradient), and a headline of 2-4 words at the display step (two lines at most) is scrubbed in from 40 percent progress, set on the ground beside or below the frame with a 56px gap. The frame then holds. Linear against scroll with 0.1 smoothing. Phone: shrinks to 70 percent of the width, frame 4:5, headline below it. Variant: instead of a centred frame the picture shrinks and slides to the right half (ending about 648 x 765 at 1440 with the page margin on its right, radius 0 to the dealt corner), and the ground it uncovers carries a text block on the left half: a headline of two lines at most at the display step, a one-line sub at the lead step and the dealt button, in place once the picture has settled.
phone: Shrinks to 70 percent width, 4:5 frame, headline beneath.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. The frame is a picture in the dealt corner, not an outlined box; the headline sits on the ground beside it, so no text box lies on a photograph; ground changes are flat colours; one picture in the page's one grade; the pin is two screens at most.

name: Grows from small
description: A vertical list of 3-5 rows, each one photograph (a frame full width inside the page margins, about 1296x680 at 1440, the dealt corner) with its title at the display step, one line, above it. As a row enters, the frame scales from 0.2 to 1.0 about its centre (scrubbed, 0.4s smoothing) between 100% and 55% of the viewport height, so it opens like a window from a thumbnail to full width; the title is fixed in place and unaffected. Inside the frame the image sits at 112% height and drifts 6% vertically as the row passes. A one-line caption (body step) sits bottom-left under the frame. The dealt section space between rows. Large scale range, no pin. Ground and ink as dealt, accent none. Phone: scale 0.5 to 1.0, drift 4%, frame 4:5 full width.
phone: Frame 4:5 full width inside the page margins; scale 0.5 to 1.0 and drift 4%; titles at the head step above.
houseRuleCheck: No numbering on rows; no overlay boxes on the photographs; captions sit on the ground, not on the picture; one title per row, two lines at most.

name: Inset grows to full bleed
description: A section placed just after the hero, with the dealt gap above it so the first screen stays the hero alone, pins for 150-200vh. A small inset (25-30% of the viewport width, 4:5 or 16:9, centred, or in the left third with a statement beside it) grows by scrub to cover the whole viewport (width and height to 100vw by 100vh, the dealt corner animating to 0) while the text beside it fades out by 30% of the progress. The side clips close and then the next section's flat ground rises over it. At full size a one-line headline at the head step may appear at the bottom-left directly on the picture's calm part. The statement beside the inset is a headline at the head step, two lines at most. Colour roles: flat ground, the picture is the colour, type in the lighter of the ground and the ink, on the picture's calm part.
phone: The inset starts at 70% width 4:5 and grows to 100vw by 100svh; pin 140vh; with reduced motion show the picture at full size with no pin.
houseRuleCheck: It is never the hero itself, because a hero that starts small breaks the full-screen first view; the headline sits directly on the picture with no box and no gradient scrim; the statement beside the inset is a headline, not a paragraph over 36px.

name: Wordmark flies into the frame
description: The nav carries a live-text wordmark. A pinned stage of 200vh holds a centred picture frame (about 640x800 at 1440, the dealt corner). Over about 900px of scroll a clone of the wordmark travels from the nav wordmark's place to the frame's centre, growing to the display step as it goes, and over the last 20% of the travel it fades into the picture while the picture scales 1.0 to 1.2 inside its fixed frame. When the pin ends the clone returns to the nav wordmark's place. The wordmark sits on the photograph as type only, in the ground colour or the light ink as contrast needs, on the picture's calm part; ground around the frame as dealt, accent none. Phone: frame full width at 4:5, the same travel from the nav wordmark's place.
phone: Frame full width at 4:5 inside the page margins, the wordmark at the display step; the same travel from its place in the nav; reduced motion: the wordmark fades in place.
houseRuleCheck: The wordmark must be live text in the page's own display face, not a drawn mark or an icon; it grows to the display step only, never a giant name (not in the footer, not larger than the headline), and it does not repeat the hero headline.

name: Pinned stage shrinks
description: A pinned stage (100svh, 0.8-1.2 viewport heights of scroll) that closes the hero. The hero's content group (a headline at the display step, two lines at most, and a product window at least half the screen's height, inside the page margins) scales from 1 down to 0.5-0.8 (origin top centre, with an 8-16px lift) as the next panel rises from the bottom over it: a flat panel in the ink field with the dealt corner on its top edge, holding the next section's heading at the head step and one body-step line, in place. Scroll-linked with 0.1 smoothing. The stage unpins once the panel covers the screen. Phone: the group shrinks to 0.7 only, the panel rises over it with 16px margins.
phone: Group shrinks to 0.7, panel rises with 16px margins.
houseRuleCheck: Clean when flat: the rising panel is a flat fill, never a gradient. The product window stays one frame (the page's one window), not boxes inside boxes, and it keeps the page margins as it shrinks.

name: Polygon clip opens
description: A pinned scene of about 900px of scroll (one screen), scrubbed. A photograph starts as a skewed polygon: clip-path polygon(8% 14%, 100% 0, 92% 86%, 0 100%) on a 573x322 box centred on the stage, rotated -4deg. As the scrub runs it grows through three sizes (573x322, then 900x480, then the full content width at 560px high, inside the page margins) while the polygon's points ease to a plain rectangle with the dealt corner and the rotation to 0. The clip-path string is rebuilt from the progress value on every frame (no CSS transition). A headline above it (two lines at the display step) scrolls up and out over the same range. Ground flat, the page's own; the photograph is the only colour. After the end state the picture holds 200px of scroll and releases.
phone: Skew halved (4% offsets), stages 320x200, 340x300, then the full width minus the page margins at 56svh; rotation limited to -2deg.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: video (a photograph only), the 40px margin (the page margin holds) and the 64px headline (display step). The polygon is a mask, not a drawn shape; no caption sits on the picture.

name: Rounded tile goes edge
description: A picture tile (16:9 or 21:9, 1370px wide at 1440) sits inset by the page margin on each side with the dealt corner as the section arrives. Over the next 650-720px of scroll (while it is sticky, or as its top travels from 90 to 30 percent of the viewport) it widens to the full 1440px: clip-path inset(0 var(--margin) round var(--radius)) to inset(0 0 round 0), the height holding or growing from 80svh to 100svh. The corner eases to 0 so it ends edge to edge. Text for the section sits below the tile and is simply there (the dealt entrance decides whether it arrives); no caption sits on the picture. Phone: inset by the page margin with the dealt corner, widening to the full 390 over 60 percent of the scroll distance.
phone: Inset by the page margin, widens to full width over 60 percent of the distance.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. A picture tile in the dealt corner, no outline, no caption box on the photograph; the pin, if any, is under two screens.

name: Blur-zoom pulse between slides
description: A full-screen slideshow of three images on a held stage of 250vh, about 80vh of scroll per slide. When the scroll crosses the next slide's threshold (or an arrow key or the dealt button is pressed) the current slide's image scales from 1 to 2 and blurs from 0 to 16px over 200ms (ease-in) under a flat black veil rising from 14% to 25%, while its text fades out; at the midpoint the next image (also at 2x and blurred) swaps in and both reverse to scale 1 and blur 0 over 500ms (ease-out); the title (display step, bottom-left) then rises through a mask. Every picture is sharp at rest; the blur lives only inside the pulse. The step plays as a timed move so the pulse reads as a camera thump; the wheel is never captured and the page keeps its native scroll. Colour: ground = the image, light ink on its calm part, accent none. No dots or counters. Phone: scroll steps it; zoom 1.5, blur 8px.
phone: Native scroll steps it; zoom 1.5 and blur 8px; reduced motion: crossfade.
houseRuleCheck: The veil is a single flat layer, never a gradient; no slide counter or numbered dots; text sits on the image as type only, on its calm part; the steps follow scroll position, with no wheel capture; the blur is a 700ms transition and every picture is sharp at rest.

name: Zoom-out fade in
description: A full-bleed photograph section, 100svh tall, with a heading at the display step, left-aligned at the page margin, in the ink that contrasts with the photograph. As the section enters (from 100% to 30% of the viewport height) the photograph fades from 0 to 1 and eases from scale 1.2 to 1.0, scrubbed with 0.5s smoothing; the heading stays fixed in front and rises 20px. Only if contrast needs it, a flat black scrim at 40-55% under the heading only, never a gradient. After it settles the photograph sits still. The words sit on the picture's calm part, in one tone, at every width. Ground around the picture as dealt; accent none. Phone: scale 1.12 to 1.0, heading at the head step.
phone: Scale 1.12 to 1.0, heading at the head step bottom-left; reduced motion: static photograph.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict. The heading is type on the photograph, no box behind it, on its calm part; no gradient fog.

name: Shrink, tilt, lift away
description: A pinned gallery stage, 250vh for three works. Each work is a photograph cropped to a panel (about 520x680 at 1440, the dealt corner) centred on the ground. Per work: the picture shrinks from full-bleed to the panel (scale 1.0 to 0.46 over the first 40% of its slot), then the panel tilts back 15deg on the X axis (perspective 1200px) and lifts away upward, fading, while the next panel arrives from below in the same shape, untilting from -15deg. The work's title (head step) swaps by a mask rise. Depth comes from the perspective only. Phone: panel 78vw, tilt 10deg, 200vh.
phone: Panel 78vw, tilt 10deg, 200vh pinned; reduced motion: plain stacked panels.
houseRuleCheck: A plain panel with no decorative notch; no shadow under the lifted panel and no outline; the picture is the panel (no box over a photograph, no card in a card); full-bleed at the start, inside the page margins at rest.

name: Slow push-in
description: A hero or section photograph (cover fit, inside an overflow-hidden frame) scales slowly once, as motion inside the picture: 1.0 to 1.06 over 10s with cubic-bezier(0.61,1,0.88,1), starting when the page has loaded (the picture itself arrives with the dealt entrance). Only scale and a drift of at most 2% in x or y; put the transform-origin at the subject (for example 32% 40%), not the centre. No words sit on the picture: the headline stands on the ground beside or under it. Use on a modern, sharp photograph or a generated picture. Static under reduced motion.
phone: Same push over 8s, scale 1.04.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the flat ink layer under text (a scrim on a photograph), so no text sits on the picture. No documentary or archive photographs.

name: Subtle grow crossing
description: Every picture in a layout breathes slightly: the image inside a fixed frame (overflow hidden, so the frame never changes) scales from 1.00 as it enters at the bottom to 1.04 as it leaves at the top, linear and scrubbed with 0.2s smoothing. Nothing else moves. Use it under static layouts where other motion would crowd: gallery strips, two-up pictures, card photos. Frames keep their layout sizes and gaps (for example 4:5, about 636px wide in a two-up at 1440 with a 24px gap, inside the page margins). Phone: scale 1.00 to 1.03. Ground and ink as dealt, no accent; the effect needs no extra type or chrome of its own.
phone: Scale 1.00 to 1.03; reduced motion: none.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict; a quiet basic that stays under the viewer's notice.

name: Title grows as the camera descends
description: A pinned stage of 250vh with a WebGL scene. A centred title in DOM (two words at the display step) scales by 1.5x (by transform) while the camera descends from a high view to a low one (its height falling to about a seventh of the start over the pin) above a flat ground plane. Four to six matte flat-colour planes (like sheets of paper, in the surface tone and the ink, the accent on one only) roll in from the sides and settle as a floor as the camera comes down. Ground = the canvas colour, ink = the title. No lighting gradient: materials are unlit flat colours, no soft shadows. When the pin ends the stage lifts away at half speed under the next section. Phone: the title at the head step growing 1.5x, canvas DPR capped at 1.5.
phone: Title at the head step growing 1.5x; same camera descent with DPR 1.5; without WebGL or under reduced motion show one static render with the title at full size.
houseRuleCheck: The planes are modelled flat colour surfaces, not drawn shapes or an illustration; keep them flat-shaded (no gradient, no shadow at rest) and limit the palette to ground, one surface tone, ink and one accent. It needs a WebGL scene the page must build itself.

name: Velocity squash
description: A horizontal row of 6-10 photograph tiles (each about 380x480 at 1440, the dealt corner, 20px gaps) moves by scroll: a section pinned for at most 250vh that maps vertical scroll to translateX. Scroll velocity is read each frame and smoothed (lerp 0.1); each tile's scale is 1 minus 0.015 times the clamped velocity (0 to 1), so tiles shrink about 1.5% while the row moves and ease back in about 0.5s (a critically damped spring, stiffness 120, damping 22, no overshoot) when it stops. A near-invisible cue that makes the row feel physical. The row starts and ends inside the page margins. Tiles are photographs only; ground as dealt.
phone: Tiles 72vw wide, native horizontal swipe with no pin; velocity from the touch gesture; reduced motion: none.
houseRuleCheck: No drag rail, scroll-progress bar or counter alongside the row; tiles are photographs, never outlined; the scroll stays native (the pin maps native scroll, no wheel capture).

name: Alternate side slide
description: Three or four rows, each full width inside the page margins (about 1296px at 1440): one big photograph tile (560x560, the dealt corner) and a caption block (a title at the head step and one paragraph of about 20 words at 20px, 44 characters wide) filling the other half, so no row is empty at the left. Odd rows put the tile on the left, even rows on the right. As a row crosses from 90% to 50% of the viewport height the tile slides 180px into its place from its outer side and the caption 180px into its place from the opposite side, scrubbed, both fully visible throughout; at rest both are in place. Every row sits on the same ground, with no second fill. The dealt section space between rows. Phone: tile above caption, each moves 40px from alternating sides.
phone: Tile above caption, full width inside the page margins; each moves 40px from alternating sides; reduced motion: no movement.
houseRuleCheck: The tile is a photograph, never a digit or a headline in a card (no 01/02/03 numbering); no outlined tiles; no row left empty on one side; scroll-linked, nothing starts hidden.

name: Side cards fan out
description: A pinned stage of 250vh. Five photograph cards (each about 360x480 at 1440, the dealt corner) start stacked at the centre; as you scroll the outer four fan outward (the two on the left go to x -400 and rotate -23deg, the two on the right to x +400 and rotate +23deg, all scale 0.76, scrubbed) while the centre card stays upright and full size. A title (display step, two words) wipes in behind the cards through a hard elliptical clip-path (radius from 0 to 120% of the stage width, no feathered edge) between 30% and 80% of the pin. Ground and ink as dealt, no accent. Phone: three cards, fan to +/-120px at 14deg, title at the head step.
phone: Three cards instead of five, fan to +/-120px at 14deg, title at the head step; reduced motion: the fanned end state, static.
houseRuleCheck: The ellipse is a hard clip, not a soft gradient mask; the cards are photographs on the flat ground, never on a photograph; no shadows between the overlapping cards (separation by the picture edges); the fanned end state stays inside the page margins.

name: Scrubbed frame sequence
description: A pinned stage (sticky, 100svh, 200-250vh of scroll) holds a canvas that draws one of 90-120 pre-rendered frames (1600x900 webp, 60-120KB each, cover fit), or a video whose currentTime tracks progress, lerped 0.1 so it glides. The subject is a product turntable, a machine opening, a pour, a growing form, rendered on the page's flat ground colour so it blends with no box. Two or three short beats (a headline at the head step, at most 12 words, two lines at most) change with progress at 20%, 55% and 85%, placed to the left or right of the subject, never over it. Preload the first 20 frames, stream the rest and show frame 0 as the poster. A packaged product can tell its unboxing this way: the sealed pack opens, the pieces part and the product rests centred while a headline of three to five words stands beside it. Colour roles: ground = the render's background tone exactly, ink contrasting, accent on the dealt button at the end.
phone: A 4:5 or 9:16 set at 960px wide (about 60 frames), pin 160vh, beats at the head step below the subject; with reduced motion show the key frame and the beats as static blocks.
houseRuleCheck: Render with no cast shadow or glow on a flat ground (no shadows at rest, no gradient backdrop); text stays beside the subject, never on it; the pin is cut to 200-250vh. Dealt only where the page has a rendered clip or frame set.

name: Gooey pill swell
description: Three or four filled bars in a centred column 1100px wide (inside the page margins), each 96px tall with the dealt corner, each holding one feature phrase at the sub step (sentence case, a few words). The bars begin as 16px dots clustered at the column's centre and swell in sequence to full width as you scroll (scrubbed over 500px), merging gooily on the way: the group of bare shapes (no text inside) runs through a blur-10 plus colour-matrix threshold filter that fuses neighbours, and the phrases are separate siblings that fade in at 80% of the swell so the type is never blurred. Once every bar has settled the filter is removed so the edges are crisp at the dealt corner; it returns in reverse when leaving. Fills: the surface tone with the ink on it, and the accent on one bar at most; ground as dealt. Phone: bars 64px tall, phrases at the lead step, column full width inside the page margins.
phone: Bars 64px tall with the phrase at the lead step inside the page margins; the filter dropped on low-power devices (bars simply scale); reduced motion: settled bars.
houseRuleCheck: Bars are filled (never outlined) and take the dealt corner at rest; the SVG filter is a rendering effect on flat shapes, not a drawn illustration, and is removed at rest; type is never filtered; no wall of tiles in several fills.

name: Headline shrinks to the corner
description: A pinned stage of 250vh on one flat ground (the ink field, or the page ground on a dark page). A two-word headline at the display step (one line, centred, in the colour that reads on that ground) slides in from the left (x -30vw to 0, opacity 0 to 1) over the first 25% of the pin, then steps from the muted tone to its full colour (a brief lift in tone in place of a glow), then blurs 0 to 10px between 30% and 50%, then shrinks and travels to the top-left corner at the page margin, unblurring, to become the section's heading at the head step, which stays while the content beneath it reveals. It never ends smaller than the head step and is sharp at rest. Phone: the headline in two stacked lines at the display step, corner target at the page margin.
phone: Headline in two stacked lines at the display step; corner target at the page margin; reduced motion: headline already in the corner.
houseRuleCheck: A tone lift instead of a glow (no glow, no shadow, no gradient); the blur is transient and ends sharp. The corner line is the section's heading at the head step, never a tiny uppercase label or an eyebrow; the dark field is one ground.

name: Hero exits on scroll
description: During the first screen of scroll the hero's content leaves. The headline scales 1 to 0.86 (or shrinks toward the top-left to 0.4x), lifts 80px and fades to 0, while the backdrop (picture, clip or canvas) scales 1 to 1.06 and dims under a flat black overlay from 0 to 40%. Supporting text and small elements go first (done by 40% of the range), the headline last (60%). The next section's flat ground then arrives from below with a hard edge. The range is 100vh of scroll, scrubbed (lerp 0.1) and reversible. At rest the hero is a full 100svh with nothing of the next section visible. Colour roles: ground = the backdrop, type in the ground colour or the ink, whichever reads on the backdrop, accent on the dealt button only. Variant for a video hero: the hero is sticky inside a wrapper 720px taller than the screen; the footage scales 1.0 to 1.2 under a flat black veil rising to 35% while the headline and button fade and lift 60px over the first 400px, then the next section slides over as a flat-ground sheet.
signature: At rest a full-screen hero; over the first 100vh of scroll the headline shrinks to 0.86, lifts 80px and fades out while the backdrop zooms to 1.06 and darkens to 40%, supporting text leaving first.
phone: The same ranges at 0.6x distances; with reduced motion no movement.
houseRuleCheck: The hero still fills the first screen alone at rest, and the overlay is a flat tone, never a gradient; designed out: the blur on the video layer (pictures are never blurred).

name: Mask counter-moves
description: A pinned scene of about 1800px of scroll (two screens), scrubbed. A window (overflow hidden, the dealt corner, 520x680 at 1440, right of centre at x 760) holds a taller photograph (520x1180). As scroll runs the window travels from translateY +250px to -250px while the picture inside travels the opposite way, -250px to +250px, so the picture seems nailed to the page while the window slides across it and uncovers new parts. A headline of two lines at the display step on the left half (from the page margin) drifts against the window at 0.5x, and a one-line caption at the lead step stands under it from the first frame. After the range the window releases and scrolls away normally. Flat ground, ink as dealt.
phone: Window the full width minus the page margins, 60svh high, travel +/-120px, caption under it.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the caption that rose in (it stands there from the first frame), the 120px headline (display step) and the 2000px pin (two screens). The headline stays on the left half outside the window, so no text sits on the photograph.

name: Object follows a path
description: A pinned stage of 250vh on the ground. A cut-out product photograph or render with a transparent background (about 260px across at 1440) travels along an invisible smooth curve (a cubic Bezier through three or four waypoints that zigzag across the stage, for example x 22%, 70%, 30%) as you scroll, turning to the curve's tangent within 12deg. At each waypoint it eases to rest for 15% of the progress while the text block on the opposite side (a title at the head step and one line at the lead step) turns from the muted ink to full ink beside it, so no side is ever empty. Nothing is drawn along the route; the object alone shows the way. Phone: a gentle zigzag down the centre, object 140px, text under it.
phone: Zigzag down the centre, object 140px, text beneath the object at each stop; reduced motion: object static beside the first block.
houseRuleCheck: No drawn route (a dashed path would be a drawn line) and no sticker or icon: the traveller is a real cut-out photograph or render and the route is invisible; the object stays inside the page margins.

name: Object flies to the corner
description: A pinned stage with a product cut-out (about 640px wide at 1440, centred) on the ground. When the next panel (a full-width sheet on the ground) rises over it, the product shrinks to 1% over the first 80% of that 700px of scroll while travelling to the bottom-right corner (x +44vw, y +36vh) with a slight roll of 20deg, and lands on the dealt button that sits there (the buy action), which gives one small bump (scale 1.0 to 1.08 to 1.0, 300ms). The sheet then covers the stage. Colour: ground and ink as dealt, accent on the button only. Phone: the dealt button is a full-width bar at the bottom edge, above the dock if the page deals one, and the product flies to its centre.
phone: The dealt button as a full-width bar at the bottom edge (52px high, above the dock if there is one); the product flies to its centre; reduced motion: product fades while the sheet covers it.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict; the product must be a real cut-out photograph or render, not a drawn illustration; the landing target is the dealt button, not an outlined box, and its bump is its only feedback.

name: Outgoing blurs back
description: A pinned sequence of 3 statements, about 600px of scroll per stage (two screens in all), on a flat ground. Each statement is a short headline at the display step, two lines of about 18 characters, centred or left at the page margin. In the last 40% of each stage the outgoing statement lifts (translateY 0 to -120px), blurs (filter blur 0 to 7px) and fades to 0 while the next stage's flat tile (the surface tone, then the ground again) slides up from the bottom and covers it. The next statement is already on its tile, sharp, and settles into place over 400ms. Colour: the ground and the surface tone alternate, ink as dealt, accent none. Every frame of the hold shows one finished statement on one tone, never an empty tile.
phone: Blur capped at 4px, lift 120px, statement at the display step (36 to 44px).
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: three-line 56-72px statements (two lines at the display step), a photograph tile (flat tones only) and 3 to 5 stages at 720px (3 stages, two screens). The blur is on text leaving, not a glass surface, and it is gone before the next statement is read.

name: Page shreds into strips
description: A pinned stage of 200vh showing a full-bleed section (a flat colour or a photograph, a headline at the display step). A flat ink bar (full width, 28px tall) sweeps down from the top over the pin, like a shredder head. Everything above the bar is cut into 24 vertical strips (60px wide at 1440), built as clipped copies of the same layer, and each strip falls: translateY to 110vh, rotate +/-3deg, in a random order with 25ms stagger, ease-in 0.7s, revealing the next section's ground beneath. Use once per page, as a strong transition. The headline is whole before the cut starts and the next section follows at once, so no empty screen is held. Phone: 12 strips of 30px, bar 20px, 150vh.
phone: 12 strips of 30px, bar 20px high, 150vh pinned; reduced motion: the next section simply covers the stage.
houseRuleCheck: The bar is a flat filled shape (no outline, no shadow); the strips are slices of real content, not drawn shapes; no torn-paper edges are drawn.

name: Product rises into scene
description: A pinned scene of about 840px of scroll, scrubbed, for a product handoff. Stage: the section's flat ground, a back layer (a cut-out of the product's setting such as a plinth, hand, shelf or stand, 640px wide, moving at 0.5x) and the product cut-out (a transparent PNG, about 520px tall at 1440) which starts below the bottom edge (translateY 110%) and rises into the setting (resting at the centre or at 60% of the width) over 70% of the range, easing out. A two-line title at the display step stands from the first frame, lifts 60px and fades out over the first 40% as the product rises, and a two-line caption at the sub step is in place by 75%. Colour: ground flat, ink as dealt, accent on one caption link.
phone: Product 62vw wide, rising over 70svh; caption below the product.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the foreground foliage layer (one setting cut-out is enough) and a title that fades in (it is there from the first frame). Cut-outs are clean present-day product pictures, never documentary photographs; no box on the pictures.

name: Big shape rises over
description: A scrubbed section handover over 720 to 900px of scroll. Section A is pinned. A flat circle (CSS border-radius 50%, 660px at 1440, in the next section's ground colour) starts below the bottom edge, centred, and rises into the screen while scaling 1 to 5 so by the end it floods the viewport and becomes the next section's ground. Section A's text stays above it until the circle passes its baseline, then fades over 20% of the range. Scrub with a 0.12 lerp. Colour: the circle is the next section's ground (the surface tone, or an ink field), ink flips on the next section; the accent is never this ground. Variant: on a picture section the same circle opens at the picture's focal point and widens by a hard clip-path circle to cover the screen over about 840px of scroll while the headline fades; the next section's headline is already there as the ground settles.
phone: Circle 120vw wide, scale to 4, 600px range.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: the image or video inside the circle, the 14px blur on the picture and the headline rising through a mask. Only a plain CSS circle that ends as the next flat ground; no outline, no gradient, no wavy edge.

name: Split headline gap
description: A headline of 2-4 words at the display step (two lines at most) is cut into a left half and a right half, both in the same ink, face, weight and size. They start together on one line, 40-60px apart. Over a pin of 0.9-1.2 viewports the halves move horizontally apart by 130-430px each while behind them a picture opens in the centre (clip inset from 50 percent to 0, or width from 0 to 360px to the content width) on a layer under the type. Each half moves as one piece; the letters never move on their own. In the last third the halves leave through the sides (x +-60vw) and fade, so no word stands next to the picture at rest and the picture ends alone. Reverses on the way back up. Phone: the halves become two stacked lines that move up and down around the opening slot.
phone: Two stacked lines move up and down around the opening slot.
houseRuleCheck: Clean with care: a picture inside a headline is banned, so the picture is a layer behind the type, opens between the halves only in motion, and the words are gone before it settles, never inline between the words at rest. Both halves share one style; no accent word; no letter animation; the pin is about one screen.

name: Collapsed stack spreads
description: Four filled bars (each 320x88 at 1440, the dealt corner, one phrase at the sub step in sentence case) begin collapsed on the first bar's position at half scale, then spread as you scroll (scrubbed over 600px) to a staggered diagonal cluster, each offset 180px right and 96px down from the one before (up to 536px of travel from the stack), growing from 0.5 to 1.0. The words inside rise 12px through masks as each bar lands. Fills: the surface tone on the ground with the ink on it, the last bar in the accent; no third tint. The cluster stays as the section's content; a paragraph (lead step, 44 characters) stands at the left, top-aligned with the first bar, so the left of the section is never empty. Phone: spread vertically 0, 72, 144 and 216px.
phone: Bars 64px tall, spread vertically at 0, 72, 144 and 216px; reduced motion: spread state.
houseRuleCheck: Bars are filled, never outlined, and take the dealt corner; no tiny uppercase labels inside them; one surface tone plus one accent bar, never several tints; the cluster is balanced by the paragraph so no row is empty at the left.

name: Titles swap by scale
description: A pinned list of 3 or 4 titles, about 450px of scroll per swap (two screens at most), scrubbed. The current title sits at the left (from the page margin, vertically centred, display step, one line, full ink). The next title grows from scale 0.5 to 1 into that spot from the lower left while the previous one shrinks from 1 to 0.4 and slides to a stack at the right margin (titles at 0.4 scale and 70% ink, 28px apart, never under 16px tall letters) that rises 120px per swap. Behind them each title has its own flat ground that wipes up from the bottom over the previous one in the same scrub: the ground and the surface tone in turn. Colour: ink flips by contrast, accent none. Titles are words only: no numerals, indices or counters beside them.
phone: Titles at the display step (about 40px); the previous shrinks into a stack at the top right (scale 0.5); 360px per swap.
houseRuleCheck: Designed out: a tonal family of grounds or picture grounds (the ground and the surface tone in turn), the 0.2 scale stack (type under 13px) and 4 to 7 titles at 650px (3 or 4 at 450px). Words only, no numerals; the stack keeps the page margin.

name: Stacked scene clip-wipe
description: Three or four full-viewport scenes are stacked and fixed in a pinned stage of 250-300vh. The first sits at rest and each incoming layer wipes up from the bottom by clip-path (inset(100% 0 0 0) to inset(0)) over about 70vh of scroll, scrubbed (lerp 0.1), while its inner image counter-shifts 10-15% (translateY 15% to 0) so it feels uncovered rather than slid. Each scene is a full-bleed photograph or a flat colour (the dealt ground, the surface tone or the ink field) with a headline at the display step (two lines at most) at the bottom-left, rising 24px with the wipe, and a body-step line. Flat scenes alternate with photograph scenes. Colour roles: scenes bring their own colour, type in the ground colour or the ink, whichever reads on each scene, accent none.
phone: The same stack at 100svh, wipe over 70vh, headline at the display step; with reduced motion the scenes are plain full-screen sections.
houseRuleCheck: Text sits directly on the picture's calm part with no box; alternate flat-colour scenes with picture scenes so the stack does not read as a heavy block of photographs; the pin is cut from 300-500vh and four to six scenes to three or four.

name: Staircase to a line
description: A pinned stage of 200vh on the ground. Three words in the display face at the display step start on a descending staircase (word one at x 8%, y 20%; word two at x 30%, y 44%; word three at x 52%, y 68%). Scrubbed, their x and y converge onto one centred baseline (y 50%, gaps 0.3em) so the three stairs become one line, the way a sentence settles; then it holds for 20% while a supporting paragraph (lead step, 44 characters) beneath it turns from the muted ink to full ink. Ink as dealt, no accent, no styling of any single word. Phone: three lines stacked as a staircase (24px steps) that align to a left-aligned stack at the display step.
phone: Three lines in a 24px staircase aligning to a left-aligned stack at the display step; reduced motion: the settled line.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict; no word is styled differently from the others and nothing is numbered; the headline ends as one line of three words, two lines at most at every width.

name: Text chunks cross
description: A centred cut-out figure or object (a picture about 560x700 at 1440 with a transparent background) and a headline split into two chunks (each one word or a short phrase at the display step) that cross it in opposite directions as you scroll through 100vh: the first chunk travels from x -200 to +200 in front of the picture, the second from x +200 to -200 behind it, so the second chunk reads as passing behind the figure. They begin offset to each side, align in the middle, and part again; the whole headline reads at the start and the end. Ground and ink as dealt. Phone: travel +/-80px, headline at the head step, picture 70vw.
phone: Travel +/-80px with the headline at the head step; picture 70vw wide; reduced motion: chunks resting either side of the picture.
houseRuleCheck: Text over a picture is fine as type, but keep it clear of boxes; the picture is a designed or generated cut-out, not a documentary photograph; the headline is two lines at most.

name: Tilted sheet levels
description: A pinned 100svh video hero. The next section, a sheet on the ground with the dealt corner on its top corners, rises over it from below, tilted 2deg about its left end at the start, and levels to 0deg as its top edge reaches 20% of the viewport height (scrubbed across 100vh). Meanwhile the video dims from 0 to 30% through a flat black layer and drifts up 8%. Type roles: the hero headline (display step, light ink, bottom-left at the page margin) lives on the calm part of the video and fades as the sheet covers it; the sheet opens with a heading at the head step at the page margin. Colour roles: ground = footage, then the sheet's ground; ink light on the video and the page ink on the sheet; accent only on the dealt button in the hero. Phone: tilt 1.2deg, 80vh.
phone: Tilt 1.2deg over 80vh; reduced motion: sheet slides over level.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict; the dimming layer is a single flat black layer, not a gradient; no shadow on the rising sheet (the colour change defines its edge); the hero fills the first screen alone and the sheet appears only on scroll.

name: Video mosaic halving
description: A split section: a list of five phrases on the left (the sub step, 24px gaps, the muted ink for inactive and full ink for active, both at 4.5:1) and a 640x640 canvas on the right that draws a playing clip as a mosaic of flat squares sampled from the video. The active step sets the square size, halving per step: 128, 64, 32, 16, 8 pixels, then the clean picture, so the footage comes into focus as you move down the list; cross-fade between sizes in 300ms. Scrub-linked (each step takes 18vh of scroll in a pinned section of at most 250vh) or hover-linked on a desktop pointer. Ground: the ink field, or the page ground on a dark page; type in the colour that reads on it; accent none. Phone: canvas sticks at the top at full width by 60vw, list below.
phone: Canvas stuck at the top (full width inside the page margins, 60vw tall), list below at the head step; step by scroll; reduced motion: the clean picture, list unchanged.
houseRuleCheck: The squares are a rendering of the footage, not drawn shapes; no monospace labels, no counters on the steps, no accent fill behind the active word; type is the page's own face.

name: Photo window morphs between shapes
description: A split stage: a list of four phrases on the left (the sub step, 20px gaps, the active one in full ink and the others in the muted ink at 4.5:1) and on the right one photo window (about 560x560) whose clip-path (an inset with the dealt corner) tweens in 0.6s (ease-out-expo) between four states when the active phrase changes by hover or click: wide and short, tall and narrow, square, and a window cut off-centre to one side. At the tween's midpoint the photo swaps (crossfade 0.3s) to the phrase's own picture. The ground stays one flat tone. Every state is a crop of a photograph with the dealt corner, never a standalone filled shape. Phone: the list becomes stacked rows at the head step above the window at 80vw.
phone: List as stacked rows above the window (head step), window at 80vw; tap steps the state; reduced motion: swap without tween.
houseRuleCheck: Each state only crops a photograph with the dealt corner (angular polygons would break the one corner radius); never a standalone filled shape (a drawn shape), no outline, no decoration; one ground, no colour steps; if the builder cannot hold a photograph in the window do not use this pattern.

name: Lines tilt in 3D
description: A headline of two lines at the display step (about 10 words, ink, left-aligned at the page margin, marked up as h2) in a section with perspective 1200px. Each line sits in its own wrapper and, scrubbed by scroll (from 85% to 40% of the viewport height), goes from rotateY(-55deg), translateZ(-120px), translateY(30px) and opacity 0 to flat, in place and fully visible; the second line lags the first by 15% of the progress, so they hinge open one after the other like pages. Transform-origin left centre. Ground as dealt. Phone: rotateY -35deg, headline at the head step.
phone: rotateY -35deg, headline at the head step; reduced motion: lines in place.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict; no word is styled differently from its line; two lines at most; scroll-linked.

name: Arc letters pop
description: A short phrase of 14-22 characters set at the display step in the display face along a gentle upward arc (radius about 1400px, spanning roughly 40deg, about 900px of chord at 1440). Each letter is its own absolutely positioned span, rotated by its angle on the arc (about -20deg at the left end to +20deg at the right), so the baseline curves. The pop is a style of arrival: it plays only where the dealt entrance lets content arrive (each letter scales 0.6 to 1.0 and fades 0 to 1, 40ms apart, 0.5s ease-out-expo, no overshoot); otherwise the phrase is simply there. The whole phrase is also one aria-label and the letters are aria-hidden. Ground as dealt, ink one colour, accent none. Phone: radius 600px, the head step, 36deg span.
phone: Radius 600px, the head step, 36deg span; reduced motion: letters already in place.
houseRuleCheck: Type on a curve is not a drawn shape and no SVG path is shown; positions are computed in script; letters stay live text in the page's own face; the arrival belongs to the dealt entrance, never a second one.

name: Brackets close in
description: A single word or two short words set large as the section's statement (display step, display face, ink, centred), flanked by two bracket glyphs from the same face at 1.2x the word's height. Scrubbed by scroll (from 85% to 50% of the viewport height) the brackets start 300px further out on each side and slide inward until they sit 0.2em from the word; the word itself is always fully visible. After landing everything holds still; a paragraph (lead step, 44 characters) sits 56px under it. Ground as dealt, accent none. Phone: word at the head step, brackets travel 120px.
phone: Word at the head step, brackets travel 120px; reduced motion: final state.
houseRuleCheck: Never a small bracketed label above a heading (an eyebrow): the brackets are typographic marks around the large statement word itself; the page's own face, never a monospace; brackets stay ink, not a styled accent; scroll-linked, so the dealt entrance stands.

name: Char blur scrub
description: A short headline of at most 10 words at the head step on two lines (or a statement of 14 words at most at 36px or less on three lines), ink on the ground, split into characters. It is scroll-linked (0.6 smoothing) over 400-720px of scroll as the block travels from 85 to 40 percent of the viewport: each character comes into focus from blur 4-12px to blur 0, staggered left to right and line by line so the focus runs like a wave of three to five letters. The text is in full ink and in place from the first frame (nothing fades or moves in; arrival is the dealt entrance's): only the focus changes. On the way out the same values reverse once the block passes 20 percent from the top. It is fully crisp before it has to be read. One type step, no colour change per character. Phone: blur peaks at 8px, splitting limited to 80 characters to protect the frame rate; the parent keeps an aria-label with the whole text.
phone: Blur peaks at 8px, at most 80 split characters, aria-label on the parent.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. No accent word, no coloured letters; letters never move or fade in, only their focus changes, and the real words are present whole; the headline is two lines at most or the statement 36px or less on three lines.

name: Colour wave through the headline
description: A headline of two lines at most at the display step, ink on the ground. A wave of the accent colour runs through every character from left to right as the section crosses the screen: scrubbed by scroll from 80% to 40% of the viewport height, with a window of about eight characters in the accent at any time (each character turns accent as the wave reaches it and eases back to ink after it passes). The wave covers the whole headline equally, so no word is singled out, and at rest the headline is one plain ink colour. Phone: the head step. Colour roles: ground as dealt, ink one value, accent the page's single accent (used only in the wave). The headline is set in one weight and size so the wave is the only event.
phone: The head step, wave window of six characters; reduced motion: plain ink, no wave.
houseRuleCheck: Flashing only the emphasised words would make a styled accent word, so the wave passes through every character equally and ends in plain ink, leaving nothing emphasised at rest; it follows scroll, never a timer.

name: Words light with the film
description: A split section: a film (a 60-90s edit or a few clips, 720x420, the dealt corner, looping, muted, with a single play/pause control that takes the dealt button) on one side and a statement of 12-14 words at 32-36px on three lines on the other. The words start in the muted ink (4.5:1) and each lights to full ink when the film's currentTime passes its timestamp (an authored array of times); at the loop everything resets to dim. Nothing is driven by scroll. No scrub bar is shown. Ground and ink as dealt, accent on the button only. Phone: film on top at full width (16:9), statement under at the lead step.
phone: Film on top at full width inside the page margins (16:9), statement under at the lead step; reduced motion: all words at full ink and the film paused on a poster.
houseRuleCheck: No on-screen progress bar or timecode; the control is the dealt button, not an outline; text does not sit on the footage; the statement is a paragraph at 36px or less on three lines.

name: Beats swap in place
description: A pinned text stage (100svh, 2-3 viewport heights of scroll in all). A block 560-720px wide at the left third holds one beat at a time: a headline of 3-8 words at the head step (two lines at most) and optionally one body-step line. With three or four beats, about 0.7 viewport of scroll each, the current beat fades to 0.1 opacity and scales to 0.9 (or blurs 6px, or drops 9px) while the next rises 9-24px from below into the very same spot to full opacity, the two overlapping by 30 percent. One picture at the right swaps in step with the beats (clip wipe from the bottom, 600ms), a different picture for each beat and each shown once, so the right side never sits empty. Phone: the block stays at the top of the upper half, the picture below it, 520px of scroll per beat.
phone: Block above, picture below, 520px of scroll per beat.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. No beat counters, no dots or progress rail tracking the beats, each beat at most 8 words, a picture keeps the right side filled, and the whole pin is at most three screens.

name: Letters drop and unskew
description: A hero word or short title (display step, display face, one ink colour) whose letters drop in from above in random order: each letter travels from -60vh to its place with skewX from 70deg to 0 and scale 0.6 to 1.0, 0.9s ease-out-expo, 40ms apart, 1.2s in all, landing on one shared baseline. It is a style of arrival: it plays once and only where the dealt entrance lets the first screen arrive; under 'already there' the word simply stands finished and this move is dropped. The letters carry no outline or shadow. Ground as dealt, accent none. Phone: the display step, drop 40vh. Use it only as the hero title or a closing statement, never as the footer's name. Set at normal tracking (-0.02em) so the word does not jump when the last letter lands.
phone: The display step, drop 40vh, same random order; reduced motion: letters already in place.
houseRuleCheck: Used on the hero headline or a closing statement, never a giant name in the footer; no shadow beneath the letters as they land; the dealt entrance decides whether it plays at all; the word reads whole once landed.

name: Letters slide from the side
description: A hero title (display step, display face, ink) that scales from 1.3 to 1.0 over 1.4s (ease-out-expo) while its opacity goes 0 to 1 in the first 40%. 400ms after it starts, a one-line sub (lead step, 24-34 characters) slides in under it, each letter 230px in from the left with a fade, 18ms stagger, 0.9s ease-out-expo, so the line sweeps in like a wave. It is a style of arrival: it plays once and only where the dealt entrance lets the first screen arrive; under 'already there' the title and sub simply stand finished and this move is dropped. Ground a flat tone or the hero picture; ink as dealt, or light on the picture's calm part; accent none. Phone: title at the head step, letter slide 120px.
phone: Title at the head step, slide 120px, stagger 14ms; reduced motion: no move.
houseRuleCheck: The sub is a sentence-case line at the lead step, not a tiny uppercase label; nothing sits in a box; the dealt entrance decides whether it plays; the title is two lines at most.

name: Line clip wipe
description: A statement of two lines at the display step (about 10 words, ink, left-aligned at the page margin, marked up as h2), not pinned. Each line is wiped in left to right by a hard clip (clip-path inset from 100% on the right to 0), scrubbed by scroll as the section crosses from 80% to 40% of the viewport height, the second line starting 20% of the progress after the first and taking 40%. Edges are hard, not feathered. Lines already wiped stay in full ink; the last line is the same ink as the rest. Phone: the head step, lines wrap but keep the stagger.
phone: The head step; wrapped lines keep their stagger (each wrapped line is its own wipe); reduced motion: all lines visible.
houseRuleCheck: The clip edge is hard (no feathered gradient mask); no word in the statement is accented; two lines at most at display size, not a paragraph; the section is as tall as its content (no pin, no empty hold).

name: Line fade-rise
description: How a heading or paragraph is split for the dealt entrance when that entrance lets text arrive: each line is its own unit, found by measuring the real wrapping and split again on resize, with no clip mask, so descenders are never cut. Where the entrance lets text arrive, the lines arrive with the dealt entrance: heading lines rise 30px and body lines 10-14px while opacity goes 0 to 1 over 800ms on cubic-bezier 0.19, 1, 0.22, 1, staggered 80-120ms, once. Where the dealt entrance is already-there, nothing arrives and this pattern is not built. Phone: 600ms, 8px, same stagger.
phone: 600ms, 8px rise, same stagger.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. It adds no entrance of its own: arrival is the dealt entrance's, and under already-there it is not built.

name: Mask roll swap
description: When a state changes (a slide, a tab, a disc, a list item) the text that describes it, a title, a price, a date or a one-to-three-word value at the lead, sub or head step, rolls out and the new text rolls in. The old text moves up 100 percent out of a mask that is exactly one line tall plus 0.1em at the bottom so descenders survive, in 300-420ms on cubic-bezier 0.77, 0, 0.18, 1; the new text enters from below 60ms later, words staggered 30ms. Labels beside it slide 12-23px. If the new title wraps to two lines the container animates its height in the same 300ms. The roll follows the direction of navigation (next goes up, previous goes down). It plays only after the visitor's own action, never on load or on scroll. Phone: the same, 260ms.
phone: Same roll, 260ms.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. The mask only clips the text itself, no outlined box; whole words roll, never single letters; it runs only after the visitor's own action, so it is not an entrance.

name: Scattered letters assemble
description: A heading of one to three words (display step, ink) whose characters begin scattered, each at a fixed pseudo-random offset of 60-120px in x and y and +/-12deg of rotation at 40% opacity, and settle to their places as the section scrolls in (progress from 85% to 55% of the viewport height, scrubbed with 0.5s smoothing), so the heading reads whole from the middle of the screen up. The same seed per character gives the same scatter each visit. The section clips overflow so the scatter stays inside it. The paragraph below it is simply there (the dealt entrance decides any arrival). Ground as dealt. Phone: offsets 40px, the head step.
phone: Offsets 40px, the head step; reduced motion: assembled.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict at rest; one ink colour, no styled word; the heading is whole from the middle of the screen up, so a stopped scroll never leaves broken words.

name: Scrubbed character mask rise
description: A headline of one to three words at the display step in which every character sits inside a line-height mask. As the section crosses the viewport the letters rise by scroll: each starts 240px below (hidden by the mask) and moves to zero between 85% and 50% of the viewport height, with a stagger of 2% of the progress per character; once risen the word stays whole and never sinks back. Ground and ink as dealt. Phone: the head step, rise 120px.
phone: The head step, rise 120px, same stagger; reduced motion: letters in place.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict; one colour; the mask is invisible, not a drawn shape; the word reads whole at rest and never sinks back out of view.

name: Scroll ink fill
description: A statement of 18-24 words at the sub step or smaller (36px at most, leading 1.2, three lines in a column of about 880px, left aligned on the page margin) rests in ink at 45% opacity, already readable (3:1 or better). As it crosses the viewport (block top at 80% to block bottom at 40%) each word goes to 100% ink in reading order, smoothed 0.15. It is not pinned: it scrolls with the page, so the fill finishes as the last line reaches about 45% of the screen height. The section holds the dealt gap above and below and nothing else. Colour roles: flat ground, ink, dim ink = ink at 45%. All words use the same fill so none is singled out.
phone: 24px on four lines, same word by word mechanism; with reduced motion show full ink at once.
houseRuleCheck: No accent word: the whole statement fills in one ink and the dim state stays readable. Designed out: the 36-56px paragraph (a paragraph statement stays at 36px or less on three lines) and the pinned variant with a picture.

name: Scrubbed line rise
description: The lines of a statement (three lines at 36px or less, or a two-line headline at the head step) are spread apart at first and close up to their leading as the block travels from 90 to 50 percent of the viewport: counted from its resting place, the first line sits 45px low, the second 90px, the third 135px, and they reach 0 offset one after the other. Every line is fully inked and visible from the first frame (nothing fades in; arrival is the dealt entrance's): only the offsets close. Linear against scroll with 0.1 smoothing, no mask, no pin. Phone: the offsets halve.
phone: Offsets halve, same scrub.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. Text never fades or arrives; the block only closes up as it comes to rest. The statement is 36px or less on three lines, or a two-line headline; no pin.

name: Word cycle with its own photo
description: A two-line headline (display step, ink, left at the page margin) whose last word cycles through four words: the old word rolls up through a mask and the new one rises in (0.6s, ease-out-expo). It runs once through the four words, 2.2s apart, when the section is half in view, then rests on the last word; it never loops. Beside it, at least 64px away and never inside the headline, one photo window (320x400, the dealt corner) swaps to the picture for that word at the same moment by a vertical wipe (clip-path inset from the bottom to the top, 0.7s). The cycling word is the same ink and weight as the rest of the line. Pauses on hover. Phone: the photo window sits above the headline at full width by 220px, headline at the head step.
phone: Photo window above the headline at full width by 220px, headline at the head step; reduced motion: the final word with its photo.
houseRuleCheck: No picture inside the headline: the photo window is separate and spaced from the text; the cycling word is not styled or coloured differently from the rest; the cycle runs once and stops (no timer loop); the headline is two lines at most.

name: Word rise stagger
description: How the words of a headline (display or head step, two lines at most) are split for the dealt entrance when that entrance lets the headline arrive: each word is an inline-block with no mask, so nothing is clipped. Where the entrance lets text arrive, the words arrive with the dealt entrance: each rises 40-80 percent of a line height from below while fading from 0 to 1 over 700-900ms (cubic-bezier 0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), staggered 50-70ms per word, once. Where the dealt entrance is already-there, nothing arrives and this pattern is not built. Phone: the same, 20 percent faster.
phone: Same, 20 percent faster.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. All words in one style; none picked out in accent. It adds no entrance of its own: arrival is the dealt entrance's, and under already-there it is not built.

name: Words tumble in
description: How the words of a headline (display step, 3-6 words, two lines at most) arrive when the dealt entrance lets the headline arrive: each from its own offset (up to 40px sideways or vertical), tilt (-27 to +27 degrees) and scale (0.45 to 1.3), the rotation sign alternating per line, all at opacity 0. They settle to exact position, 0 degrees and scale 1 in 900-1100ms on ease-out-expo (no overshoot), staggered 70-110ms in two to five groups, once. The end state is perfectly aligned and crisp. All words keep one colour. Where the dealt entrance is already-there, nothing arrives and this pattern is not built. Phone: offsets and tilts halve.
phone: Offsets and tilts halve.
houseRuleCheck: Clean. One colour for all words; no accent word; nothing stays tilted at rest. It adds no entrance of its own: arrival is the dealt entrance's, and under already-there it is not built.

name: Words zoom through
description: A pinned stage of 250vh on one flat ground (the ink field, or the page ground on a dark page). Three words or short phrases (display step, in the colour that reads on that ground, centred) pass through the viewer one after another: each grows from scale 0 and blur 16px to scale 1 and blur 0 over 45% of its slot, holds sharp for 10%, then grows to scale 2.2 with blur rising back to 16px and opacity to 0 over the last 45%, so it flies past. The next word begins as the last leaves, overlapping by 10%. The last word holds and the pin releases onto a paragraph. Phone: the head step, phrases of up to two lines. Variant: a statement of up to 10 words in two lines at display size assembles in place instead of flying past: its words arrive from scale 1.3, blur 8px and opacity 0 in a shuffled order across 60% of its window, hold for a quarter of it and leave the same way before the next statement arrives. Split by words, never by characters, so every word reads whole.
phone: Phrases up to two lines at the head step, 200vh; reduced motion: words stacked in a normal section.
houseRuleCheck: No conflict; blur applies to the words only and ends at zero; no counter or numbering of the words; each word is whole at its hold; the dark field is one ground.

name: Hero video loop
description: The hero stage is 100svh and a muted, autoplaying, looping clip (cover fit, 1920x1080, under 3MB, 6-20s, poster = its first frame) fills it, with nothing of the next section visible. Footage is motion graphics, product macros, abstract material or rendered scenes, not documentary footage; for a clip with cuts use 3-5 shots of 2-4s. Over it, directly on the footage's calm part with no box: a headline at the display step (two lines at most) at the bottom-left on the page margin, in the ground colour or the ink, whichever reads on the footage, a lead-step sub of at most 40 characters, and the dealt button beside it. If the words need help, pick a calmer part of the clip or lay a flat black scrim at 40-55% under the words only, never a veil over the whole clip and never a gradient. A body-step text control, Pause, sits bottom-right on the page margin. Colour roles: ground = the footage, type in the ground colour or the ink, whichever reads on the footage, the accent only on the dealt button.
signature: A looping clip fills the whole first screen (100svh) with the headline at the bottom-left on its calm part, the dealt button beside it and a text Pause control at the bottom-right: no centred headline, no card, no next section peeking.
phone: Serve a 720x1280 crop, or only the poster on data saver; headline at the display step at the bottom, button full width; playsinline autoplay; with reduced motion show the poster.
houseRuleCheck: No gradient scrim (a flat veil at most), no documentary footage, and the text sits directly on the footage with no box. Dealt only where the page really has a clip.

name: Poster with a play button
description: A film block: a poster frame (16:9, about 960x540 at 1440, taken from the clip, the dealt corner) with the dealt button centred on it (a filled button, never a ring, its label reading the word Play and the length). On hover the dealt button gives its own feedback and the poster scales to 1.03 (0.4s); on click the poster fades out in 0.4s, the clip starts with sound and the button disappears; native controls appear after. Nothing else is on the poster. Phone: poster full width inside the page margins, the button at its phone height, no autoplay.
phone: Poster full width inside the page margins, the dealt button at its phone height, tap starts playback with sound, no autoplay; reduced motion: same, no hover scale.
houseRuleCheck: The dealt filled button, never a play ring (an outlined shape); no icon-only glyph; the button is a control on a picture, not a card on a photograph.

name: Autoplay video tiles
description: A grid of 4-6 filled cards in the dealt card style (3 columns by 2 rows of about 410x520 at 1440, 32px gap, dealt corner) in which each card's picture is a muted looping clip (6-10s, 720p, 600-900KB, poster = first frame) running to the card's edges, with a lead-step title and a one-line body-step text beneath on the card fill (the surface tone). A clip plays only while at least 50% visible and pauses otherwise, with at most three playing at once. Hover steps the card fill one tone; no shadow. Colour roles: flat ground, cards on the surface tone, ink, accent on a closing link.
signature: Each card's picture is a muted looping clip that plays only while at least half visible (three at once at most), with its title and one line on the card fill beneath.
phone: One column of cards at full width inside the page margins, clips play at 60% visible and only on wifi, posters otherwise; with reduced motion show posters.
houseRuleCheck: Captions sit on the card beneath each clip, never on the footage; footage must not look documentary; every card has the one surface fill and the grid is not the only thing on the page.
